title: Automated checks on the core flows
summary: Every change now runs a browser through the flows students and admins rely on most, so a broken reservation, kiosk return or shift trade is caught before it ships.
details: Covered: reserving gear and picking it up and returning it at the kiosk, kiosk walk-ups with admin edits to the checkout, shift claims, approvals and trades, time off approval, and the Wrapped countdown.
The confirm step of a new reservation showed the event's time in the wrong time zone when the page was first loaded; it now shows Madison time like everywhere else.
Nothing else changes in what you see.

title: Bug hunt follow-ups: availability, contacts, bulk assign
summary: Five more findings from the web bug hunt are closed: late-night availability blocks now count, staff contact details stay out of student reads, reservation edits follow the same start rules as new reservations, and bulk assignment keeps every pick that still fits.
details: Availability blocks are checked on every day a shift touches, so a game that runs past midnight no longer misses a block early the next morning, and all-day events check the event's own weekday.

Students and collaborators no longer receive staff and admin phone numbers, athletics emails or birthdays through the user list and profile responses; student contact details stay shared with the team.
Moving a reservation's start now follows the same rules as creating one: not into the past, and not beyond the advance-booking window.

Applying a bulk assignment now stages every pick that still fits and reports the ones that no longer do, instead of refusing the whole batch when one person was reassigned or deactivated after the preview.
The test-notification buttons send at most a few pushes per minute.

title: Faster, cheaper calendar subscriptions
summary: Your subscribed shift calendar is now answered from a cache, so the thousands of overnight refreshes calendar apps make no longer wake the database.
details: A subscribed feed refreshes from the cache until the schedule actually changes, then rebuilds on the next poll.
Calendar apps that already have the latest version get a quick "nothing new" reply instead of the whole file.
Old links from a reset or revoked calendar token stop reaching the database.
Nothing changes in what your calendar shows.

title: Bug hunt: accounts, times, checkouts
summary: A sweep across the web app closes several account-safety gaps and fixes reports, checkouts and schedule actions that behaved wrong at the edges.
details: Role and email changes are tighter: staff change student roles only, personal API tokens can't change emails or passwords, and a changed email ends any pending reset link.
Forgot-password sends at most a few links per address per hour, and a leftover role preview no longer blocks signing back in.
App Activity counts each day in Madison time, so afternoon and evening use no longer shows under the next day.
Cancelling an open checkout no longer restocks units already reported lost, and merging checkouts keeps every item on the chosen return time.
A crew member on a multi-day event can be approved for a timed shift on one of its days, and shifts on cancelled events can't be posted for trade.
A student's edit of approved time off goes back for review, and the time-off notes behind the assign picker are staff-only.

title: iPhone catches up with the website
summary: The iPhone app now shows the department Wi-Fi, lets admins change items on an active checkout, and names every scan and item change in a booking's history.
details: Find the Wi-Fi network and password under Shared logins, with a QR code to show someone else.
Admins can add an available item from a checkout's menu, or swipe an item to take it off. Taking off the last item closes the checkout.
Booking history names each item scanned out or back in, with a run of scans shown as one line.
Staff can open All shifts on a person's profile to see every shift they've been on, upcoming and past.

title: Clearer purchase matches
summary: Budget suggestions now flag equally supported item matches for review.
details: Matching records with the same purchase evidence are marked as possible matches.
Admins can compare the records before linking an item.

title: Clearer budget planning
summary: Budgets now distinguish unknown amounts from recorded zero and keep a saved plan for comparison as purchases change.
details: Save or revise a plan without later edits changing its baseline.
Review missing amounts and purchase statuses before relying on totals.
Find inventory using stronger purchase evidence and open linked items directly.
Choose the number of bulk items when linking a purchase.

title: Staff command line and API tokens
summary: Staff and admins can now create personal API tokens in Settings > Security and use the new wc command line, or its MCP server, to view and edit the schedule, handle trades and call any app action. AI agents like Claude can use it too.
details: Tokens act as you, can be read-only, and expire.
Sign-in, passwords and account changes stay browser-only.
Times always show in Central.
Fixed: Active sessions in Settings > Security showed none.

title: Approve trades right on the Schedule
summary: Admins now see a "to review" button on any event with a claimed trade or an open-slot request, and can approve or decline it without leaving the Schedule.
details: Works on every row of the Schedule list, on desktop and phone.
One button covers all the trades and requests for that event.
Approving is paused while an event has unreleased crew edits, same as before.

title: See the Schedule by person
summary: Staff can switch the Schedule week to By person: one row per student with their shifts, hours and can't-work times for each day.
details: Tap a name for their week: shifts, hours against the team average, trades and availability.
All shifts shows every shift they have been on, upcoming and past.
A shift that overlaps a time the student can't work is flagged.
Students with no shifts stay in the list so you can see who is free.

title: Different position labels for each half
summary: On the Schedule, one person can now carry several position labels, such as SLOW1 for the first half and CAM3 for the second.
details: Open a person's label on the crew editor and tap Add another; pick Full game, 1st half or 2nd half for each.
Every label shows next to their name on the Schedule and the event page.

title: Onboarding checklist on student profiles
summary: Admins can see on each student's profile how far they are through onboarding, and tick off the in-person steps.
details: Photo, phone, student details, sizes, class schedule, guides, app install, notifications and first checkout fill in by themselves, with the date each happened.
Slack, Asana, computer login, Adobe, building access, orientation and gear training are ticked by an admin and show who did it and when.
Wiscard is shown but optional. Nothing is emailed to the student.
Each admin step can show who to contact and a note, and admins can tick a step for a whole group at once.
Adobe access finishes itself once they claim an Adobe license.

title: Schedule changes show up within seconds
summary: When someone adds or removes a person on a shift, everyone with the Schedule open sees it within about ten seconds, with no refresh.
details: Covers shift assignments, trades, crew edits and publishing.
The page checks quietly only while you are looking at it and pauses when you step away.

title: Cleaner Shared logins, plus Wi-Fi
summary: Shared logins has a calmer, easier-to-scan layout, and the department Wi-Fi now sits at the top with a QR code you can scan to join.
details: Scan the Wi-Fi QR code with your phone camera to join, or tap it to show it larger and print a sign to tape up.
Copy the Wi-Fi network name or password with one tap; the password stays hidden until you show it.
The open-site button on a login copies its password and opens the site, ready to paste.
Each login shows its site, email and password in one tidy block; long lists get search and category sections.
Software pages now use the refreshed look.

title: Simpler Kits list
summary: The Kits list shows just the kits.
details: The status strip above the list is gone; each kit still shows Ready or how many pieces are out.
Rows open the kit when clicked, so the separate Open column is gone.
Contents read as one plain line, like 9 assets + 3 item families.

title: Tidier profile summary
summary: The top of a profile is shorter and calmer.
details: Performance shows on-time returns, checkouts and badges side by side instead of stacked.
Open schedule and See all are quiet gray links instead of blue.

title: Easier-to-read Reports
summary: Report breakdowns read like a ranked list, and the Most-used gear chart shows its numbers.
details: Breakdowns by location, category, type and department show a soft bar behind each row instead of ruled table lines.
Most-used gear prints each item's days in custody at the end of its bar, so you don't have to hover.

title: Search finds gear by brand and model
summary: Cmd-K search now shows every item that matches, including matches on brand or model, in one tidy line each.
details: Searching for "sony" or a model name used to hide items whose tag didn't contain the words. They show now.
Each item reads as tag, product name, then status, with the holder's avatar when it's out.
Checkouts, reservations and people take one line each, with the name on the right.

title: Quieter Notifications inbox
summary: Notifications read like a simple inbox: what happened, when, and a red dot for anything new.
details: Tap a notification to open what it's about. The check mark marks it read.
All and Unread tabs replace the summary strip, and days group under Today, Yesterday and This week in Central time.
The Unread and Read tags and the per-row buttons are gone.

title: Cleaner Schedule list
summary: Schedule rows say each thing once, and the phone layout gives more room to events.
details: Each event shows its open seats once, with the crew as avatars beside it.
On phones, event rows drop the repeated date and sport name, and Auto assign sits beside the title.

title: Tidier Bookings lists
summary: The Bookings list lines up better and is easier to use on phones.
details: On phones the All, Checkouts and Reservations tabs get their own row instead of being squeezed out by the view controls.
In list view, rows that can't be selected no longer shift their columns out of line.
Overdue bookings keep the red badge and edge, and the title stays in normal text.

title: Calmer Items pages
summary: Items has status tabs with counts and shows who has each item and when it's due back.
details: Tabs across the top filter by status: Available, Checked out, Reserved, Pending pickup, Maintenance and Retired.
The status column names the person holding the item and its due time, in Central time, with overdue items in red.
On an item's page the header keeps one main button, a favorite star and a More menu (Report a problem, Refresh and staff actions).
The active checkout card shows who has the item and when it's due back.

title: The paint roller is back
summary: When you add something weekly, you can paint the days and hours onto a week grid like the old WhenToWork roller, in red.
details: Tap Paint it in on Add something weekly, then drag across the days and hours.
It fills in the same days and times as before; you still name it and save.

title: A complete, clearer activity log
summary: Every scan, swap and change now shows in the history of the item and booking it touched, in plain sentences, and admins can filter the log by area and person.
details: Booking and item history now show each item scanned out and back in, with bursts of scans folded into one line that names every item.
A swapped or removed item keeps those events in its own history, and swaps name both items.
Edits show what changed (old value to new value) instead of raw data.
Password changes and signing out other devices are now recorded.
Reports > Audit has Area and Person filters, and kits have a History card for staff and admins.
All dates and times in the activity log and across the app show in Central time.

title: Neutral buttons and tab underline
summary: The app's main color is now neutral near-black instead of blue, and tab bars show a single underline under the active tab.
details: A second, shorter red underline no longer sits on top of the first one, and the active-tab underline is now neutral dark instead of blue.
Primary buttons, selected states and focus rings are near-black in light mode and light gray in dark mode.
Fixed on the Item, Bookings, Licenses and Bulk inventory pages.

title: Trades tab and calmer link colors
summary: Trades now live in their own tab on Schedule, and links and body text are neutral instead of blue.
details: Schedule has a Trades tab next to List, Week and Calendar, with the open-trade count on it.
Trade Board is no longer in the More menu.
Links and secondary text use neutral colors across the app.
The underline under the active tab no longer gets clipped in scrolling tab bars.
Menus and dropdown lists have larger rows on phones and tablets.
Opening the app with an expired sign-in now goes to the login page instead of an error.

title: Admins can manage active checkouts
summary: Admins can now add or remove gear on, or cancel, a checkout that is already out, without going to a kiosk.
details: Open the checkout and tap Add items, then search and pick an available item.
Use the menu on an item row to remove it. Taking off the last item closes the checkout.
Cancel is now available on an active checkout. Everything on it is released as returned without a scan.
Admin-only actions are shown in a red-to-violet gradient.
Each change is recorded in the activity log.

title: On shift now follows game time
summary: The Staff page no longer lists crews hours before a game that was added without a time.
details: Crews that kept an old all-day window now use the game's real start and end until calendar sync catches up.
The same rule applies to the live badge on a person's profile.

title: Team availability for staff
summary: Staff can now see when every student can't work, week by week, on one page.
details: New Availability tab under Staff shows each student and each day of the week.
Pending requests show dashed so they are easy to spot.
Click a student to open their full availability.
On iPhone, staff get a Team Availability screen under Users with a day picker.

title: Remove broken gear from a kiosk pickup
summary: Gear that went into maintenance no longer blocks removing other items, or picking up the rest of a case.
details: Removing an item from a reservation no longer re-checks everything else on it, so a case with several items in maintenance can be trimmed down.
When a kiosk pickup is blocked, it now names the item and who has it instead of saying "Availability conflict".

title: Fix call times on newly timed games
summary: Games that got their real time after being listed by date only now show the right crew times.
details: Crews no longer keep a leftover all-day window like 6:00 PM – 6:00 PM once the game has a time.
This stops false schedule conflicts that blocked students from claiming other games the same day.

title: Calmer event titles on Schedule
summary: Event names in the Schedule list are plain text again instead of bright blue, so the page reads quieter and the game info stands out.
details: Titles underline when you hover them, the same as before.
The small label under a title, like Exhibition, is now a soft gray.

title: Faster pages on slow connections
summary: Most pages download about 30% less code, and Home, Bookings and Staff now arrive with their content already in place, so they show up two to three times sooner on a weak connection.
details: The Schedule page, the biggest one, loads about a third less, and its list draws only the layout for your screen, so a busy season opens noticeably sooner.
Dialogs like Auto assign, Add item and Invite people download only when you open them.
Tab underlines, fade-ins and small icon changes now play right away instead of waiting for the page to finish loading.
Home, Bookings and Staff no longer wait for a second round of loading before showing your gear, bookings and people.

title: Fix On shift now list
summary: The Staff page no longer shows people as on shift before their shift starts.
details: Games with no set time yet no longer put the whole crew on shift the night before.
A personal or slot call time now decides when someone counts as on shift.
Students and staff both show, and the end time uses Madison time.

title: Fix false shift conflict when claiming
summary: Claiming a shift no longer says you already have one just because you are on a multi-day event.
details: A crew spot on a multi-day all-day event, like a tournament, no longer blocks claims on every other game during those days.
Single-day events and shifts with a set call time still count as conflicts.

title: Fix License and Profile loading
summary: Licenses and some coworker profiles failed to open in the iPhone app. Both load again.
details: The Licenses page shows who holds each seat again.
Opening a collaborator's profile from the directory works again.

title: Auto assign explains itself
summary: Auto assign always fills every slot it can, and shows each sport's default.
details: The “Full crews only” switch is gone. An event with a slot nobody fits is still filled for the rest, and you can uncheck any single assignment in review.
A sport that fills both staff and student slots is now labeled “Staff and students,” so it no longer sounds like the crew toggle.
If something changes while you review (a request, time off, another edit), Auto assign now stages everything that still fits and tells you how many it left out, instead of asking you to start over.
Staff and admins, who can be double-booked, are no longer skipped just for having another shift at the same time.
“This semester” from December 21 to 31 now runs through spring instead of a full year ahead, and the event dates in the dialog use Central time.
Review has a Change button on every assignment that offers the next best people for that slot, so you can swap someone without leaving Auto assign.

title: Checkout report shows the right day
summary: Clicking a day on the checkout report heatmap now labels the list with that same day.
details: The day chip and the "Checkouts on" title used to show the day before the one you clicked.
Auto-fill previews now name the sport on hold, like "Volleyball", instead of a short code.
Gear availability checks for consumables now run one shared query, so both checks always agree.
Database health in Settings now checks every database update this version ships, and flags failed or unknown ones, instead of an old fixed list.

title: Equipment picker tabs no longer double up
summary: Each item in the equipment picker now appears on exactly one tab, the same one its count is shown under.
details: An item with a known category always appears on that category's tab, even when its type mentions something else, like a camera battery grip.
Items without a category are sorted by their type, using the first matching tab, so a camera battery no longer shows on both Cameras and Batteries.
Removing someone from a sport roster who was already removed now returns a clear "not found" answer instead of a server error.

title: One password-change path
summary: Passwords can now only be changed through the protected Change password form, which limits repeated tries and signs out your other apps.
details: An older, unused way to change a password has been removed.
Every password change now goes through the same rate-limited check and signs out the Mac and iPhone companions.
Behind the scenes: more automated checks for sign-in sessions, push alerts, schedules, the dashboard and trade alerts.

title: Safer item photo links
summary: When you add an item or battery family photo from a link, the app now checks that the file really is an image before saving a copy.
details: A link that returns a web page instead of a picture is now refused, even when the link ends in .png or .jpg.
Saved copies use the picture's real type, so a JPEG sent as PNG is stored correctly.
When a kiosk hand-off moves one item, the server's reply now reads "1 item" instead of "1 items".

title: Kiosk times in Chicago time
summary: When the kiosk says an item is booked for a shared travel case, the booking times now show in Chicago time.
details: Before, those times showed in UTC, five or six hours ahead.
Other booking messages already used Chicago time and are unchanged.

title: Clearer profile history
summary: Saving your profile in Settings now records only the fields you changed.
details: A person's activity now reads "Updated their phone" instead of counting every field on the form.
A save that changes nothing no longer adds an activity row.

title: Import and override fixes
summary: Item imports no longer turn a price like "n/a" into a zero price, and checkout overrides show up once in the audit log.
details: A price or value cell with no number in it now imports as blank.
Each admin override on a checkout records one audit entry, with the items it skipped.

title: Issues page day counts fixed
summary: The daily counts on the Issues page now follow Madison days, so evening reports land on the right day.
details: Before, a report from the evening counted toward the next day, and the last two weeks ended on the wrong day.
Photo Mechanic license reminders and replacements also follow Madison dates now.

title: Longer names fit in Profile Next Up
summary: Game and gear names on a profile's Next Up list now wrap instead of cutting off.
details: Names like “Volleyball vs Nebraska” show in full on a second line on every iPhone size.
Applies to your own profile and to a teammate's profile.

title: Audit report comparison fixed
summary: The audit report's comparison with the previous period now respects the record type you filtered by.
details: Filtering the audit report to one kind of record, such as bookings, now compares it with the same kind of record in the period before.
Before, the earlier period counted every kind of record, so the change looked larger than it was.

title: Damage report emails fixed
summary: Emails about an item reported from its own page now open the Damage page instead of a broken link.
details: Reports filed during a return still open that checkout.
The in-app alert and the email now always link to the same place.

title: Battery pickup counts fixed
summary: A battery scanned twice at the kiosk now counts once when a reservation is picked up.
details: A full pickup waits until every battery the reservation needs has actually been scanned.
Each numbered battery goes on the new checkout only once.

title: Wrapped hours and team totals fixed
summary: A dry run of the fall recap fixed how hours and team numbers are counted.
details: Shift hours now count shifts whose attendance was never logged, so hours no longer come up short.
Events without a sport are no longer ranked as an “Other” sport.
Team totals leave out collaborators, and the biggest-crew card only shows when people worked together.
Big numbers get commas, tied sports are called a tie, and long venue and sport names no longer get cut off.

title: Schedule list keeps your place
summary: Day headers on the Schedule list now stay pinned while you scroll, and loading older events no longer jumps you to a different spot.
details: The date header for the day you are reading stays visible under the Schedule bar.
Scrolling up into older events keeps the event you were looking at in the same place on screen.

title: Position tags and lost units fixed
summary: Position tags like ROAM2 and GC show in capitals again, and a lost unit can be settled right from the Dashboard.
details: Titles such as Football vs USC (ROAM2) keep their capitals in Recent activity and other lists, including ones saved earlier.
The lost-unit row on the Dashboard now opens a short list where each unit can be marked Found it or Write off.

title: Quieter background refresh at night
summary: The iPhone app no longer refreshes its widgets in the background between 10 PM and 6 AM, which lets the server rest overnight.
details: Widgets and Spotlight catch up with the first background refresh after 6 AM.
Opening the app still loads everything right away, at any hour.

title: Clearer first-week guidance
summary: New students are told how to sign in to the app, where checkouts start, and why Home has no shifts yet.
details: The setup finish screen now says to sign in to the iPhone app with the same email and password.
An empty Checkouts list explains that gear is checked out at the kiosk or in the iPhone app, and shows up here with its return time.
A new student's Home says nothing is scheduled yet and shifts appear once the team schedules them, instead of sending them to hunt for trades.

In the next iPhone app update, a new student's Home welcomes them instead of saying they are caught up, the setup fields stay clear of the Continue bar when the keyboard opens, and long empty stretches on the Schedule show their end year.

title: Tidier layouts across the iPhone app
summary: Home, Schedule, Items and Profile fit better on every iPhone size we support.
details: The Home greeting now uses the full width instead of wrapping beside your photo.
Schedule's Non-game filter is the same size as the others.
Profile's Next Up and the Items list show longer names on two lines instead of cutting them off.
Report a Problem uses the app's standard red and green.

title: Wiscard is now optional during setup
summary: New teammates without a Wiscard can finish setting up their account.
details: The Wiscard step can be skipped, so people who are not UW students are no longer stuck.
A Wiscard can still be added any time from your profile.

title: A clearer, friendlier Dashboard
summary: The Dashboard reads more naturally and the right side now shows what is really happening today.
details: The sidebar highlights in Badger red, and the Creative Wrapped preview is hidden until mid-November.
The greeting now says things like “You’re working football vs USC tonight at 6:30 PM,” and recent activity says checked out, picked up or returned, with the exact time on hover.
A shift and its gear pickup for the same event now show as one Up next row, and camera labels such as ROAM2 keep their capitals.
Working today uses call times, so a night game no longer shows as live in the morning.
Coming up labels every event Home, Away, Neutral or Non-game, and Team gear out shows avatars and sits above it.
Missing battery units can be marked found or written off right from the Missing Units report.

title: Easier to read gear details
summary: The small grey text on the UA gear pages, like colors, sizes and dates, is darker so it is easier to read.
details: Gear details now meet the standard contrast for small text.
Applies to picking gear, your kit and the staff gear boards.

title: Fewer page errors on Home
summary: Home and New reservation no longer hit a brief display error when they open.
details: The pages now wait for your device's clock before showing the greeting, date and default times.
The iPhone app's return countdown on the Lock Screen is more tolerant of how its updates arrive.

title: Photo reminder respects Not now
summary: On the iPhone app, tapping Not now on the photo step at the end of setup no longer brings the photo reminder straight back.
details: Setup still finishes when you skip the photo.
The photo reminder now waits a day, the same as Not now anywhere else.

title: A calmer Dashboard and sidebar
summary: The Dashboard is quieter and easier to scan, and the sidebar is shorter, with our apps and everyday sites one click away.
details: The Creative Wrapped banner now shows once instead of twice, and the admin preview is a small row instead of a full red block.
New reservation uses Badger red, the one brand-colored action on the page.
Section links and the Up next highlight use calm neutral styling, with colored dots for pickups and shifts.

Weekly-or-rarer staff pages (Budget, Wish list, UA Gear Picks, Badges, Signatures, YouTube Studio Lite, Issues) move into a folded More group. A dot shows when something inside needs a look, and the sidebar remembers if you leave it open.
Tools is now Apps: the iPhone app on the App Store, Offload and Fetch sit above the browser tools.

A new Quick links menu opens the sites the team uses every day in a new tab. Admins add, edit, reorder and remove links in Settings > Quick links and choose who sees each one: everyone, students and staff, staff only, or admins only.

title: Contact details on profiles
summary: Staff and student profiles in the iPhone app now show email and phone numbers, with quick Message, Call and Email buttons.
details: Hold an email or phone row to copy it.
Hold a phone row to text or call from the menu.
Your own profile doesn't show the card.

title: iPhone app: Chicago time everywhere
summary: Today, Tomorrow and every shift and game time in the iPhone app now follow Central time, even if your phone is set to another zone.
details: Your profile no longer says nothing is coming up when it simply couldn't load; it offers Try again.
Gear picks only look tappable when you need to add your size.
The New Reservation heading now grows with your text size.

title: UA gear shows everything you'll receive
summary: The UA staff gear page now opens on your picks and the gear in your kit, with photos and status, and the full catalog sits below.
details: Your gear lists your picks first, then your standard-issue kit, each with a photo you can tap to enlarge.
Pieces that still need a size are flagged so you can fix them before the order goes in.
The Catalog button jumps to the full assortment.

title: UA gear leads with your picks
summary: The UA Gear screen on iPhone now opens on everything you can expect to receive: your picks, then the gear in your kit, with the full assortment one tap away under Catalog.
details: Your picks and your kit pieces both show a photo, color, size and status, and picks swipe to remove with a Review and submit button that stays in reach.
Catalog (top right) holds the full assortment with search; picked items keep their count badge.
Items still missing a size are flagged in orange so you can fix them before submitting.
Tap any item photo to see it full size, and pinch or double-tap to zoom.

title: Clearer validation messages
summary: Form and request validation moved to a newer checker, so a few default messages read differently, such as "Too big: expected array to have <=5 items" where a limit is exceeded.
details: Fields with their own wording are unchanged; only the generic limit and type messages changed.
Error responses keep the same shape, so the iPhone app and web pages behave as before.

title: Sign with Apple Pencil on iPad
summary: Signatures are now captured in the Wisconsin app on iPad, under Browse > Signatures. The web keeps rosters, imports, previews and downloads.
details: Staff and admins on iPad get team rosters with readiness counts, search, a jersey number pad, and saved signature previews.
The signing screen shows the signer's name and number large, with Undo, Redo, Clear, Replay and Done. Ink that runs off the edge turns red so it gets redone before saving.
Saves are safe to retry, and replacing a signature another iPad just saved asks first.
On the web, unsigned rows now read Capture in iPad app, and old capture links open the roster.

title: Football scores and six new badges
summary: Football games on a profile's Scoreboard now show the final score from UW Athletics, and six new badges reward football game days.
details: Each finished football game shows Wisconsin's score first, with links to the UW and ESPN game pages.
The score is the one UW Athletics publishes. Nothing shows until UW lists the game as final.

Games also record whether the opponent was ranked, whether they went to overtime, and the TV network. Six new football badges use them: Photo Finish, Giant Killer, Top 25 Regular, Bonus Time, Prime Time and Clean Sheet.
Scores refresh once a day during football season.

title: Six new badges, three of them surprises
summary: New badges to chase, plus three hidden ones tied to Badger game days.
details: Iron Crew is for working 100 event shifts, and Centurion is for returning 100 checkouts on time.
Fifth Quarter is for working five home football games.
Three surprises stay hidden until someone earns them. Here's a hint: one is about a rivalry, one is about a homecoming, and one is about a number.

title: A badge gallery for the whole team
summary: Badges is now a gallery everyone can open. See every badge, who has it, and how your collection compares with your teammates.
details: The Gallery shows every badge and who on the team already earned each one, with Up next at the top: the three badges you are closest to earning.
The Team view shows who earned what this week and ranks everyone by badges earned. Pick anyone to see what only they have, what you both have, and what only you have.
Surprise badges stay a surprise: you can see that someone found one, but not what it is until you earn it yourself.
Badges for damaged, missing or late gear never show who holds them and never count toward the ranking.

Badges moved into the People section of the sidebar for everyone, and a profile's Badges tab links straight to who else has a badge or to a side-by-side compare. Staff still award badges from the new Award tab.
Rarity is now measured among the people who can earn badges, so collaborator accounts no longer make every badge look rarer, and the badge report no longer ranks people who have left.

title: Roster invites are emailed
summary: Adding people with Paste a roster now emails each of them their setup link, and Resend sends the invite itself.
details: Email the invite now applies to both Add one person and Paste a roster, and the result shows how many were emailed.
Resend on someone who hasn't signed up sends the normal invite instead of a reminder.

title: Skip the photo during setup
summary: The last setup step now says Skip for now when you haven't added a photo, and your profile reminds you to add one later.
details: If an earlier detail is still missing, the photo step tells you which one to go back and add.
A skipped photo shows up as a gentle profile reminder that you can snooze.

title: Clearer invite emails
summary: Invite emails are shorter, with one setup button and a link to download the iPhone app.
details: Create your account in the browser from the invite email, then sign in to the iPhone app.
Adding people now says Nothing new to add when every address was already invited or already has an account, and points to Resend.

title: Today and Tomorrow match the real day
summary: Evening games no longer show up under Tomorrow on Staff Today or the Dashboard.
details: Staff Today now counts events by the Madison calendar day, so a 7 PM match is listed under Later today and the Events today count includes it.
Dashboard Coming up and other Today and Tomorrow labels use the same Madison day, even late in the evening.
Report and export file names now carry the Madison date, not tomorrow's date after 7 PM, and a check keeps UTC dates out of user-facing code.

title: Safer sign-up and account protections
summary: Creating an account now needs the link from your invite email, and a few account details are shared only with the people who need them.
details: New accounts are created from the link in the invite email. Typed the sign-in page by hand or lost the email? Enter your address and choose Email me my invite link.
Invite links work for 30 days; a resend sends a fresh one and retires the old link. Set up in the browser, then sign in to the iPhone app.
Wiscard card details on a teammate's profile are visible only to that person, staff and admins.
When an admin resets someone's password, any passkeys on the account are cleared too, so the person sets everything up fresh after signing in with the temporary password.
Sign-in responds in the same time whether or not an address has an account.

title: Print labels sheet fixes
summary: The print sheet keeps its template headings in view while you scroll, and the P-touch CSV export no longer waits on the USB checks.
details: Camera bodies, Lenses, Batteries and other headings stay visible under the Print sheet header as you scroll.
Export CSV for P-touch Editor works whenever the sheet's selections are valid, even if the USB font or QR check is still running or unavailable.
Unplugging a scanner or another USB device no longer drops the printer connection.
Importing an older browser sheet is offered once instead of on every visit, and recovering an unreadable saved sheet works on the first retry.
Batch receipt downloads work in Safari and Firefox, and the label count is announced to screen readers.

title: A calmer Battery Ops
summary: Battery Ops is redesigned to show what is on the shelf, what is out, and what needs a look.
details: One summary at the top shows how many batteries are ready to check out, with a bar for out and missing.
A single Needs attention list gathers low families, missing batteries, stale flags, and batteries out a week or more.
Each family is one card with its count and where low starts; the unit list stays tucked away until you open it.
Checked out batteries show who has them, with their photo or initials, and how long.

title: Print labels straight to USB
summary: QR Print sends centered Gotham labels directly to the Brother printer, with larger previews and less tape waste. Print history records who printed each label and supports careful recovery after an interruption.
details: Connect the Brother PT-D610BT in desktop Chrome or Edge and print without opening P-touch Editor.
Chained batches keep the approved Medium Small QR and Gotham layout, with one initial leader instead of blank strips between labels.
Stop preserves the unsent labels; review uncertain output and continue with only the confirmed remainder.
Print history keeps the operator, label content, timestamps and recovery links. Printing and confirming labels were applied remain separate steps.
Larger previews and whole-sheet checks catch text, QR and selection problems before printing. Drafts follow the signed-in account on the current browser.

title: Continue setup on either device
summary: Your setup answers save as you go, so you can continue on the web or iPhone. Profile photos are easier to frame and retry.
details: New students complete the required contact, Wiscard, student and apparel steps before entering the app. The photo stays optional.
Confirmed answers and Getting started progress follow your account between devices, with clear recovery when answers change elsewhere. Continue waits for your latest answers to save.
Finishing without a photo records setup as complete; a photo can be added later from Profile.
Move and pinch the photo inside a circular guide, with scroll and keyboard support on web. Interrupted uploads retain the crop for another try.

title: Extend gear with Siri
summary: On iPhone, overdue alerts now come through Focus, and you can extend a checkout by asking Siri.
details: Overdue gear alerts are now Time Sensitive, so Focus and Scheduled Summary no longer hold them.
Say "Extend my checkout in Creative" to add 1 or 2 hours. Siri tells you the new return time and asks before changing anything, and it never goes past the next booking that needs the gear.
Widgets in a Smart Stack move to the top when gear is due soon or a shift is about to start, and they stay up to date even when you haven't opened the app.
An open booking can continue on your iPad or Mac with Handoff.
Choose which Creative alerts come through during a Focus in Settings > Focus > Focus Filters.

title: A cleaner Board Sizes
summary: Board Sizes makes it easier to find what a piece needs, has a calmer look with the Badger red kept, lets you preview your art on any board, and builds After Effects comps for a whole board.
details: The venue page starts with What are you making?, which leads to every board and size a piece needs, and Board terms explains venue words like FG/BG, GIP, fascia and scrim.
Search understands venue words like ribbon and ticker, and suggests matching content such as Touchdown.

Preview your exports: drop an export folder (or files) and each render lands on its board and zone by size and by name, the way exports are named (Short Wing Left, SEZ Upper, Main 1920x1080). Videos play together with sound from the main, files for other boards say where they go, and Mockup PNG saves the result. A What are you making? page shows which canvases are covered and which are missing. Files stay in your browser until you remove them.
More on a board downloads an After Effects script with a comp for the whole board and each zone size.
A calmer look in Lato with Badger red kept and the shared tool header with Apps at the top right. Ids and canvas keys hide until you turn on Technical details.
Phones get a tidier layout, copying works in browsers that block the clipboard, More menus work from the keyboard, and a broken link no longer leaves the page blank.

title: Report a Problem in the iPhone app
summary: Settings in the iPhone app now has Report a Problem, and crashes in the iPhone app, kiosks and the Mac menu bar app reach the team with what led up to them.
details: Report a Problem in Settings sends your note with the screen you're on, your app version and device, and your last few actions. Contact Support is still there if you'd rather email.
When the iPhone app, a kiosk or the Mac menu bar app crashes, the report now includes the screens and requests just before it, so problems can be fixed without asking you to retrace your steps.
Nothing you type, and no passwords, is ever included.

title: Everyone hears about gear transfers
summary: When gear changes hands, both people now get told, whoever made the change.
details: The new holder gets a notification with the due time.
The old holder sees it come off their record, and gets a notification if staff moved it.
Transferring a checkout is held while a return is in progress.
The transfer windows on the web are redesigned: a searchable list of people, a clear from and to, and a note of what each person will see.

title: Smarter low-battery alerts
summary: Battery stock and low-battery alerts are now more accurate, and big battery pools get an inbox alert when they run low.
details: Low stock is now relative: a family is low below 20% of the batteries we own, so small groups with just a few batteries no longer show as low.
Large battery pools, like Sony, send staff and admins an inbox notice when they run low, at most once a week.
Force-completing a checkout no longer puts a battery that was reported missing back into stock.
Battery suggestions for cameras no longer mix up similar models like the R5 and R50.
Adding battery units to an archived item is now blocked.

title: Simpler Accountability on iOS
summary: The iOS Accountability screen now matches the web page: gear still out, your own record, and people who are repeatedly late.
details: Overdue now sits at the top; tap a row to open the checkout.
A Your record row shows your late returns and on-time rate.
The list shows people late 2 or more times, with a button to include everyone else.
Rank numbers are gone.

title: Fill crews faster
summary: Assign several people to open slots at once, and start a crew from the sport's usual size.
details: When an area has two or more open slots, Fill picks several people at once and assigns them in one save.
Crew size shows the sport's home or away template, so you can match it in one tap or save the current counts as the new template.

title: One on-time rule across the app
summary: The on-time rate on staff profiles now matches the Accountability report.
details: A return counts as on time unless it came back after the due time plus the grace period.
A checkout still out past that point counts against the rate.
The rate only shows once someone has 3 or more completed or overdue checkouts.

title: Safer calendar and image links
summary: Links that staff paste for calendar feeds and item photos are now checked more carefully.
details: Feed and photo links that redirect somewhere unexpected are now followed one step at a time and checked at each step.
Nothing changes for normal links.

title: Photo Frame, rebuilt
summary: Photo Frame is redesigned as a calm editor with the photo on the left and every setting on the right, and it now handles a whole set of photos at once.
details: Fixed photos that showed only ISO on the frame: shutter, aperture and focal length now come through from every kind of file, including iPhone HEIC photos in Safari.
Drop up to 12 photos, give them one look, and export them all. Each keeps its own camera settings and caption.
On iPhone, Share sends the framed photos straight to Photos or Messages. Copy puts one on the clipboard.
Saves as JPEG by default (a fraction of the size), with PNG still offered.
New Border (Slim, Regular, Wide) and Text (Split or Centered) options, a light and dark look that follows the Apps page, and a warning when a long caption gets cut short.
Everything still happens in your browser. Nothing is uploaded, and location data from the original never carries over.

title: Golden Hour forecasts the light
summary: Golden Hour now forecasts the sky for each golden hour and helps plan the week.
details: Each morning and evening window has a sky outlook, like Good chance of color in the clouds or Low overcast, flat light, with cloud cover and temperature.
A Next 7 days list shows every evening (or morning) golden hour with its outlook. Tap a day to open it.
Each window says where the sun rises or sets, like Sets WSW · 255°.
Hover or drag across the sun path to read the time, light and sun height at any moment.
A cleaner look on the same full-page sky, with Badger red touches.
Custom coordinates and My location now show times in that spot's own time zone.

title: QR Studio, refreshed
summary: QR Studio has a calmer Badger red look, codes that scan more reliably, calendar event codes, and an optional caption under any code.
details: Every style now scans reliably: rounded corner eyes are redrawn, and there is a new Eye shape choice.
The scan check is stricter and flags a code that only reads at some sizes.
New Event type: scan the code to add a game or shoot to your phone's calendar.
Add an optional caption like "Scan for tickets" under the code, in PNG and SVG, without affecting scanning.
Deleting a saved code, or clearing the library, can now be undone.
Cleaner logo backings, no hairline seams, and the shared tool header with Apps top right.

title: A calmer, shareable Timelapse planner
summary: The Timelapse planner is redesigned and now lets you share an exact plan with a link.
details: A cleaner layout with light and dark mode, Badger red accents, and the viewfinder readout kept front and center.
Copy link shares the exact camera, method and settings, and Copy plan includes that link. Reset goes back to the defaults.
On iPhone, fields no longer zoom in when tapped, and a slim bar keeps the answer in view as you scroll.
Greyed-out cadences now say why, like 4K Time-lapse needing an HD format past 5 seconds.
Clearer messages when a clip needs a faster S&Q rate than the camera offers.

title: Assign shifts reads by day
summary: The Assign shifts page now lists events by day with each area's crew beside the event, instead of a wide table.
details: Names are no longer cut off, open slots show as dashed chips, and conflicts stay in amber.
The review filter shows its counts inline.

title: Schedule shows open shifts plainly
summary: Each event in the Schedule list now says Covered or how many shifts are open, with a color dot for the sport.
details: Replaces the 1/1 badge with Covered or N open.
Sport color dots match the ones in the new reservation event picker.

title: Clearer booking actions
summary: A booking now has one obvious next step at the top, with everything else under Actions.
details: Checked-out gear shows Extend as the main button, reservations show Edit, and finished bookings show Re-reserve.
Edit details moves into the Actions menu when Extend is the main step.
The booking summary and the step bar on a new reservation are larger and easier to read.
Gear photos on a booking are bigger, and the Kits filters now sit in one quiet row.
A booking page now leads with the gear list in one centered column; schedule, people and notes sit in a Details section below.

title: QR print helper for labels
summary: Print labels is rebuilt as a print helper: pick gear, choose how many, and download a CSV ready for the Brother label printer.
details: Search everything, or filter to serialized items or families, and add with one tap.
Serialized items print one label each, with copies if you need spares.
A family prints one family label, and counted stock can print one label per item on hand.
Numbered families can print a label for every unit not yet labeled, all of them for a reprint, or just the numbers you type, like 7 or 12-18, then mark them printed.
Change what a label says before printing without touching the item, and reset it to the item's text any time.
Each label previews to scale from its real P-touch template, and every CSV comes with its template to download.

title: A calmer Schedule, Reports and Notifications
summary: Schedule, Reports, Notifications, Operations, Blasts, Search, Badges, Signatures and Profile now share the fresh look.
details: Schedule keeps Auto assign up front and tucks Add event into More. Event times are easier to read.
Notifications moves Refresh, Check overdue and Preferences into a More menu, and Open details is a quiet link.
Report bar charts use one accent color instead of a rainbow.

title: Easier-to-read Bookings
summary: Booking cards on the Bookings page are larger and clearer, in the fresh look.
details: Dates and places use regular type instead of tiny monospace, and the requester's name is bolder next to their avatar.
Bookings, Checkouts and Reservations share the same fresh theme as Items.

title: A calmer Items and Kits
summary: Items, Kits, Print labels and Import now use the fresh look, with one main action per page.
details: Items keeps Add item up front and tucks Export, Import, Fill gaps, Cleanup wizard and row density into one More menu.
Available gear shows a small green dot instead of a filled pill, so checked-out gear and the people holding it stand out.
Kits shows Ready the same quiet way.
On a kit, Duplicate stays up front; Archive, Delete and the way back to all kits sit in a More menu.
On an item, the Info fields read as plain values and only show a box when you hover or click to edit.

title: Tools in the sidebar
summary: A new Tools item in the sidebar opens QR Studio, Board Sizes, Golden Hour, Timelapse, and Photo Frame in one click.
details: Hover Tools at the bottom of the sidebar, or click or tap it, to see each tool.
It works from the collapsed sidebar and on your phone, and with the keyboard.
All apps and tools at the bottom of the list opens the full page.

title: A smoother iPhone experience
summary: Profile setup has a clearer look, and everyday gear and schedule actions are easier to use. Home, Blasts and Scoreboard bring more of the team workflow to your iPhone.
details: Setup adds Wisconsin branding, clearer step progress and larger fields and buttons, with layouts for dark mode and larger text.
Home focuses on your next shift, pickups and gear, with attention messages that match your account.
Trade Board rows open details while Claim, Approve and Decline remain separate actions.
Gear search and Siri include bulk items, and scanning a gear family opens the matching search.
Staff can compose and track blasts from iPhone, and Browse includes the team tools.
Scoreboard adds filters, head-to-head comparisons and clearer results on web and iPhone.

title: Send blasts from your iPhone
summary: Staff and admins can send a blast from the iPhone app and see who has acknowledged it. Browse also gets the team's Tools.
details: Message Crew on an event sends a blast to everyone on its published crew.
Before you send, you see how many people it reaches and who they are.
Sent shows who is still waiting, who acknowledged, and lets you cancel the banner.
Golden Hour, Photo Frame, QR Studio, Board Sizes and Timelapse open from Browse.

title: My kit for UA gear
summary: Under Armour gear now has a My kit card showing what you are getting and what has been handed to you.
details: Open UA gear to see every piece in your kit with its size.
Each piece shows Planned, On order with the expected date, In hand with the date, or Add your size.
Students on the student list see their kit there too.
Your kit stays hidden until gear picks are opened to everyone.
Admins see order follow-ups under Needs attention, like late arrivals and people waiting on gear.

title: A friendlier first-day setup
summary: New students get a calmer setup after they accept their invite, and a clear place to start when it's done.
details: The sign-in and create-password pages now match the iPhone app: a calm dark surface with a single light button.
The Welcome setup now shows a simple step bar, one question at a time, and works comfortably on a phone.

When setup ends, a short list points to where to start. Onboarding Status now flags anyone who hasn't signed in or finished setup after three days, and students who haven't said when they can't work, so staff know who to nudge.
The invite email now spells out what happens next, including installing the app, and how to reset a forgotten password. Adding one student or staff member can send it right away.
New students and staff see a Getting started card on Home for their first two weeks, on the web and the iPhone app, and what they check off carries across both.

Students can add when they can't work, like classes, another job or days out of town, so they aren't scheduled then. It's optional, offered on the Getting started card, and always one tap away from Home and Schedule. If you're already on a shift then, you can post it to the Trade Board right there.

title: A calmer Bookings screen on iPhone
summary: Bookings on iPhone is rebuilt to be quieter and easier to scan.
details: The list is grouped by day, with anything overdue or waiting on pickup first.
Each row shows who has it and a colored time: red overdue, orange missed pickup, blue checked out, purple reserved.
Switch between Everyone and Mine at the top, and the filter button now says what you are looking at.
Booking details are redesigned: a status line, pickup and return side by side with a progress bar while gear is out, and the owner with their photo.
Extend shows the current and new return side by side with quick picks like 1 more hour or Tomorrow, and picking a time is one tap. Booking notes are gone from iPhone.
When gear is needed again, the booking says which booking needs it next.

title: A more balanced Home
summary: Home's two columns now end at about the same height, and quiet cards take less room.
details: Recent activity sits under Up next for staff, and Team gear out does for students, so the right column no longer runs long.
Empty cards show a short one-line note instead of a large centered block.
On tablets and smaller laptops Home is one column, so cards keep a readable width.
Rows with a Remind, Approve or Claim button no longer repeat the action as text.

title: A calmer Settings
summary: Settings has a new look and fewer pages. Notifications on the web now match the iPhone app, and your shift calendar link lives on Profile.
details: Related options are grouped into clean rows, with a visible preview for light, dark and system themes.
Notifications on the web cover every type, with Off, Silent or Alert for each, quiet hours, and a badge awards switch.
Profile has a Shift calendar section to subscribe to your shifts in Apple or Google Calendar.
Extend presets moved into Checkout policies, and calendar venue matching moved into Locations with plainer wording.
The audit log lives only in Reports, now with Record and Action filters.
Every admin page was rebuilt to be easier to scan, including Sports, which now opens one sport's crew at a time.

title: Hide gear from partners
summary: Admins and staff can now keep individual items out of the Big Ten Network and Learfield catalog.
details: Each item has a new Visible to collaborators switch under Workflow Eligibility, on by default.
Turned off, the item disappears from collaborators' catalog and they can't reserve it, including through a kit.
Staff and students are unaffected.

title: Brand assets for partners
summary: Big Ten Network and Learfield collaborators can now browse and download the brand asset library.
details: Logos, fonts and brand files are available from a new Brand assets link in the sidebar.
Internal guides and the contacts list stay hidden from collaborators.
Admins can switch this off per organization in Settings, Collaborator access.

title: Partners see team gear activity
summary: Big Ten Network and Learfield collaborators can now see what gear is booked and who has it, not just their own bookings.
details: Bookings and Checkouts show everyone's reservations and checkouts, with full names.
The Items list shows who currently has a piece of gear and when it is due back.
Brand now shows in the gear catalog for collaborators.
View only: collaborators still can only change their own reservations, and pickups and returns still happen at the kiosk.
Admins can switch this off per organization in Settings, Collaborator access.

title: A new Home page
summary: Home was rebuilt around what you need first: what needs attention, what is up next, and the gear you have out.
details: A greeting and one line about your day sit at the top, like your call time and what gear is due back, followed by four quick counts for your role.

Needs attention gathers overdue gear, missed pickups, damage and loss reports, shifts that still need gear, drafts, and (for admins) trade claims waiting on approval. Staff can send an overdue reminder right from the row, and the browser tab shows how much gear is overdue.
Up next spotlights your next shift or pickup with how soon it starts, then lists the rest by day.

Working today shows who is on each of today's events, and staff see Recent activity: the latest kiosk pickups and returns. Students can claim open trades, and admins can approve trade claims, right from Home after a confirm.
Each card loads, fails and retries on its own, so one slow part no longer blanks the page.
Partner staff get the same layout with just their gear and the published schedule.

title: A cleaner Trade Board
summary: The Trade Board is easier to scan, and students now hear when a shift they could take is posted.
details: Tabs for Review, Available, Mine, and History, with shifts grouped by day, soonest first.
Open shifts and trades from other students sit in one list with a single Claim button.
When someone posts a shift to trade, eligible students in the same area get a notification.
The iPhone app's Trade Board has the same tabs and day grouping.

title: One badge notification a day
summary: Badges you earn on the same day now arrive as one notification instead of one each.
details: When a shift, checkout or return earns you several badges at once, they're listed together, like "3 badges earned".
A badge earned later the same day joins that notification and brings it back to the top.
Badges a staff member gives you still arrive on their own.

title: Quieter, more accurate notifications
summary: Your unread count now shows what still needs you, and the app stops notifying you about things you just did yourself.
details: Notifications clear on their own once they're settled: gear returned, a request decided, an event over, or a newer schedule update for the same event.
Badge notifications clear after two weeks, so they no longer pile up in the count.
Reserving gear, merging your own reservations, or handing gear to someone at the kiosk no longer sends you a push about it.
"Gear up for your shift" is skipped when you already have gear booked for that shift or event.
Buttons in notification emails open the exact checkout or event.
Staff follow-ups about overdue gear arrive silently overnight, from 10 PM to 7 AM. The person who has the gear is still alerted.

title: Fewer unused preview databases
summary: Documented why screenshot branches still created preview databases and how to stop it.
details: Screenshot-only branches now carry a copy of the deploy settings file, so pushing to them no longer creates a deployment.
Stray preview databases from those pushes stop appearing.

title: Search kits, events and guides
summary: Search in the iPhone app now also finds kits, upcoming events and guides, each with its own filter.
details: New Kits, Events and Guides filters sit beside Gear and People.
Events search matches the title, opponent or location of upcoming events.
Results open the kit, event or guide directly.

title: Fairer, clearer crew assignment
summary: Picking crew and auto assigning shifts now explain each choice in plain words and spread work more evenly.
details: The crew picker suggests the best fits first and shows why each person fits and how busy their week is. Arrow keys and Return assign without the mouse.
Auto assign favors people with a lighter week and fewer shifts this season, instead of giving every tie to the same person.
The Auto assign review shows who goes where and why, and lets you leave single slots open when partial crews are allowed.
Assign shifts has a calmer month grid and a Student workload panel that shows who is busiest, who has no shifts yet, and highlights one person's shifts when you tap them.
Event pages have a Fill open slots button with the same review, and Crew size sets every area's Staff and Student positions in one step.
On iPhone, the crew picker matches the web: Suggested, Check first and Unavailable, with each person's week at a glance.

title: Tidier App activity people list
summary: Settings > App activity now shows each person's devices in a few clear chips and knows about iPhone 1.3.
details: Xcode and simulator builds fold into one quiet chip with the newest build and a count; hover for the full list.
The same phone on the same version shows once.
The web chip names the latest browser and counts the others instead of every browser profile.
On release day, phones on an older version show as Behind as soon as the App Store lists the new one.
The Apps page and the Wisconsin Creative app page list version 1.3.

title: Creative money for UA gear
summary: A Budget line can now count toward a year of Under Armour gear, so the UA page shows it without typing the amount twice.
details: Edit a Budget line and pick the UA year under Counts toward UA gear.
The UA gear Budget card adds it on top of the allotment and lists where it came from.
Cancelled lines stop counting. The line also gets a UA tag on the Budget page.

title: Clearer gear return countdown
summary: The gear return Live Activity on iPhone now shows a large countdown and a track that drains toward the return time.
details: The lock screen and Dynamic Island show the time left as one large figure, in hours and minutes once it is over an hour.
A thin track shows how much of the last two hours remains.
Overdue, returned and not-updating states keep their own colors and wording.

title: More widgets, smarter search
summary: The iPhone app adds Lock Screen and larger widgets, filtered search, a scan history, and easier inbox swipes.
details: Next Shift and My Gear widgets now fit the Lock Screen and come in Medium and Large lists.
Search has filters for gear, reservations, check-outs and people, with quick jumps to Scan and My gear.
The scanner keeps a short list of recent scans and hints when it can't see a code.
Notifications are grouped by day, and you can swipe to mark one read or unread.
Ask Siri to search gear by name.

title: Post trades from Schedule again
summary: On iPhone, posting a shift to the Trade Board works again, and Schedule recovers cleanly when a load fails.
details: Swipe a shift in Schedule, or tap Post on the Trade Board, to post it. Both were hidden by a status mix-up.
Shifts you already posted no longer show up to post twice.
If later or earlier weeks can't load, Schedule says so and offers Try Again instead of spinning.
Claiming a shift now says it was requested, since an Admin approves it, and Schedule updates when you close the Trade Board.
Larger text sizes keep event names, dates, and filters readable.

title: Catch mistyped booking end dates
summary: Reservations and checkouts can no longer be saved, edited or extended to run longer than a year, which catches a mistyped year before it blocks gear.
details: If an end date is more than a year after the start, you'll see a message asking you to check the end date.
Bookings of a few weeks or months work as before.

title: Quicker reviews of upcoming changes
summary: Upcoming changes can be tried out on a computer with one step before they go live, so updates get checked sooner.
details: One command sets up a private copy of a proposed change and opens it in the browser.
It uses test data only and never touches the live site.

title: A Scoreboard you can play with
summary: The Scoreboard is redesigned on the web and iPhone to be fun to explore: the team record up top, facts you can tap, and a leaderboard you can dig into.
details: Did you know cards surface stories in the season, like who has worked the most events, the team's record when someone is on crew, home versus away, and your own spot. Tap one to jump to that person or view.
Switch the leaderboard between events, wins and win rate and watch people move to their new places. Tap anyone to see their sports and record without leaving the page.
Head to head compares any two people, starting with you and the leader.
Explore lets you tap a sport, venue, opponent or site to zoom the whole Scoreboard into it. Sport chips sit at the top, and the other filters are under More filters.
Games that ended more than four months ago now stay in the season record instead of dropping out.
Every finished game is now saved with its result and crew, so the season can be replayed and recapped later even if a schedule changes.

title: Staff looks right in dark mode
summary: Staff tiles, notices and the hiring sheet now use dark-friendly colors instead of light pastels.
details: The Right now tiles, Open schedule and See all links use softer tints and brighter text in dark mode.
The org chart notice and the hiring sheet banners no longer glow against the dark page.
Light mode looks the same as before.

title: Kiosk checkouts use clean titles
summary: Checkouts started at the kiosk for a game now get the same title as everywhere else, like "Men's Soccer vs Evansville".
details: Kiosk checkouts for a game are titled with the sport name and opponent instead of the calendar's raw event name.
Reservation and damage or loss alerts show the clean booking title.
The kiosk's "needed next" card no longer cuts typed titles at a dash.

title: Simpler Accountability page
summary: Accountability now leads with what matters: gear still out, your own record, and people who are repeatedly late.
details: Overdue now sits at the top with who has what and how long it is overdue.
A Your record line shows your late returns and on-time rate.
The list shows people late 2 or more times; one-time late returns are a click away.
Location, status and sort options moved into More filters.
The podium and joke captions are gone.

title: Steadier kiosk in the background
summary: The kiosk does less needless work when you start a checkout, return or pickup, and server errors give clearer advice.
details: Leaving the home screen no longer triggers one extra full refresh of the dashboard.
A kiosk that was just signed out stops checking in with the server right away.
If something fails on our side, the kiosk now says to try again in a moment instead of asking for another scan.

title: Right now on iPhone staff profiles
summary: Staff profiles in the iPhone app now open with what someone is doing right now, followed by their week and how they're performing.
details: A new top section shows the next shift or on-shift status, what they are holding, and a badge they're close to earning.
A This week card lists their shifts with area-colored dots, and a Performance card shows on-time returns, checkouts and badges earned.
The staff list has blue role tabs, an area dot beside each person, and softer cards.

title: A redesigned Resources library
summary: Guides and Brand assets have a cleaner, calmer layout that puts the right guide or file in front of you faster.
details: Resources opens with a big search, For you guides picked for your role and area, quick tools like the Media Drive path, topics with counts, and recently updated guides.
Every guide shows how fresh it is. Editors can mark a guide verified, and guides untouched for six months say Needs review.
Reading a guide keeps related guides on the left and the contents on the right, with Edit, Copy link and Mark verified close at hand.
Writing a guide now feels like a document: a big title, the editor, and a quiet settings panel for type, audience and featuring.
Brand assets opens as a grid of previews, with one-tap file-kind filters and a list view if you prefer it.
On iPhone, Guides opens with For you and Recently updated, and every guide shows the same freshness as the web.

title: Damage and loss, tracked
summary: Report a problem with any item, any time, and staff get one page to follow every damaged or missing item through to an outcome.
details: Report a problem on any item page, on the web or iPhone: say it's damaged or can't be found, with a note and a photo.

A new Damage and loss page lists every open case with the photo, the note, who had the item, and the checkout, including lost batteries and supplies. Closed cases stay on file. Staff get the same queue on iPhone under Browse, Equipment.
Staff close a case as repaired, replaced, written off, found, or no issue. Repaired, found and no issue put the item back in service. Replaced and written off retire it.

An item reported missing, or reported damaged while idle, is held right away so it can't be booked again, and shows as Missing in the catalog. A checked-out or reserved item stays in service until staff review it.
The dashboard flags stay until a case is closed and link to the new page, and the sidebar shows how many cases are open.
A checkout now shows what was reported at return and where it stands, to the person it's for and to staff.

title: Sidebar fixes, and pins that follow you
summary: Sidebar page names show the full tails of letters like g, y and p.
details: Fixed the bottom of letters such as the g in Badges and Signatures being clipped in the sidebar.
The workspace name and your name in the account menu get the same extra room.
Pinned and hidden sidebar pages are saved to your account, so they follow you to other browsers and computers.
YouTube Studio Lite and issue pages use the shared page title, and issue pages show their title in the top bar.

title: Name and area when adding one student
summary: The Add users dialog now opens on Add one person and can start a student's profile with their name and primary area.
details: Add one person is now the first tab, and the dialog opens on it.
For a student, you can enter an optional name and primary area, so their profile starts filled in.
Pasting a roster or uploading a CSV works as before.
The Invite-only access notice no longer wraps one word per line.

title: Fewer wasted deploys
summary: Updates to the site now go live more reliably, because work-in-progress branches no longer use up the daily deploy allowance.
details: Only merged changes start a production deploy, so a day of many small updates no longer blocks the next release.
Review previews for in-progress work are unchanged.

title: Nudge people who haven't finished setup
summary: Onboarding Status can now email a reminder to someone who signed in but has not finished their profile.
details: People marked Setup needed get a Nudge button next to Open.
It asks once, then emails them a reminder to sign in and finish setup.
Each person can be nudged once a day, and people who finished setup don't show the button.

title: Remind everyone waiting
summary: Onboarding Status can now email the login link to everyone who has not signed in yet.
details: A Remind everyone waiting button sits next to the filters and asks once before sending.
It shows how many people were reminded and how many were skipped.
Each invitation can be emailed 3 times an hour, so a second tap soon after skips people already reminded.
If email isn't set up on the site yet, it says so and sends nothing.

title: A Right now row on profiles
summary: Profiles now open with what is happening with that person right now.
details: Next shift shows their next confirmed event, with the time and place. Holding lists gear they have checked out and flags overdue gear.
Almost there shows the badge they are closest to earning, and Badges shows the four most recently earned.
This week lists their confirmed shifts for the next seven days, colored by area.
Performance shows on-time returns, checkouts and badges earned. On-time means returned by the due time, and checkouts with no recorded return time are left out of the rate.
The Info tab cards now match: softer corners and bolder titles.
Students see this on their own profile, and staff and admins see it on anyone's. A tile only shows when there is something to say.

title: Get the iPhone app banner
summary: On iPhone, Safari now offers the Wisconsin Creative app from the App Store.
details: Safari shows its standard App Store banner at the top of signed-in pages. Close it and Safari remembers.
It doesn't appear on the sign-in page or once the app is installed.

title: Report a problem, and faster fixes
summary: Report a problem from the account menu, and crashes and errors now reach the team with what they need to find and fix them.
details: Report a problem in the account menu sends your note with the page you're on, your app version and browser, and your last few clicks, so you don't have to explain the steps.
If a page crashes, you can add what you were doing in one tap. The crash itself is already reported.
Crashes and errors from the web, iPhone app and server are grouped by cause, so a repeat problem is fixed once.
Nothing you type into fields, and no passwords, is ever included. Reports are deleted after 90 days.

title: Badge celebrations show once
summary: A badge you earn is now celebrated one time, no matter how many phones, browsers or kiosks you use.
details: Before, each device remembered on its own what it had shown you, so a phone or browser you hadn't opened in a while could pop up badges you'd already seen, and two open devices could show the same one.
Now the app remembers it once for your account, and badges you've already earned won't come back.

title: App activity redesign
summary: The owner-only App activity page now shows at a glance which app versions people run and how they use the site, the iPhone app, and the menu bar.
details: A Needs attention list shows who is behind, who is on an old TestFlight build, who can't get notifications, which version crashed most, and any kiosk that stopped checking in.
Charts show daily active people by platform, release adoption by version, the most-used screens, first opens by week, and crashes and hangs by version.
The current iPhone build now comes from the App Store listing automatically. Local Xcode builds and phones not seen in 60 days no longer count as behind.
The people list is one clean row per person with filters, sorting, and a link to each profile. It shows the menu bar app and which browser and device people use on the web.

title: My kit for UA gear on iPhone
summary: UA gear in the iPhone app now shows your kit and where each piece stands.
details: Each piece lists its size and whether it is planned, on order with a due date, or in your hands.
A piece with no size says Add your size and takes you to your profile.
Students on the student list see their kit there too.
Your kit stays hidden until gear picks are opened to everyone.

title: Mac app: 1Password sign-in and cleaner glance
summary: Password managers like 1Password can fill the sign-in form in the Mac menu bar app.
details: The menu bar app now comes to the front when you open it signed out, so 1Password and Apple Passwords can offer your saved login.
Picking your login fills the email and jumps to the password; the app remembers your email, so signing in again takes one pick and one Touch ID.
If your password manager's picker closes the menu, choose Sign in in a window to sign in from a window that stays open.
The message after the server ends your session now just says you were signed out.
Test, demo and simulator iPads no longer appear in System Health or turn it Critical.
Long booking titles wrap to two lines, borrower names stay whole, kiosk rows skip a location their name already says, and search waits for Command-F instead of grabbing focus on open.

title: Consistent booking titles
summary: Bookings now read the same everywhere: sport name, vs or at, then the opponent.
details: Older bookings that showed codes like "MSOC vs Evansville" now show "Men's Soccer vs Evansville" on the web, in notifications, reports, the iOS app and the menu bar.
Promotions ("- Homecoming"), rankings and "(Neutral)" no longer clutter booking titles.
Titles you type yourself, like "Media Day - Kohl Center", keep their dashes.
New game bookings are saved with the full sport name and a clean opponent from the start.

title: A calmer sidebar and top bar
summary: The sidebar and top bar look the same on every page, with clearer groups, fresh icons, pinned pages, a new account menu and the page path up top.
details: Fixed the sidebar switching fonts and styling when you opened Staff, Budget or Wish list.
New light and dark look with clearer icons and groups for People, Purchasing, Library and Staff tools. Press [ to collapse the sidebar.
Pin your most-used pages, drag them into order, or hide pages you never use from Customize sidebar in the account menu.
Search (Ctrl or Cmd+K) opens with recently viewed pages and quick actions. The account menu holds Settings, Profile, appearance and help.
Quiet counts show open wishes waiting on a decision (admins) and Software codes reported as not working (staff and admins).

The top bar shows where you are, including the name of the item you're viewing, the bell opens your latest notifications in place with an Unread view, and the phone tab bar adds a More tab. Page titles match the new look.

title: Schedule stays on the visible week
summary: The next iPhone update keeps Schedule on the visible day when only a few events are listed.
details: Short schedules keep the first visible day selected, even when several weeks fit on screen.
Today returns the list and week selection together after scrolling.
Longer schedules still follow the last visible day when you reach the bottom.

title: Swap a Photo Mechanic code
