summary: If your Photo Mechanic code won't activate, you can now get a different one without asking staff.
details: Tap Code not working? on your license, confirm, and a new open code appears right away.
The bad code is flagged for staff to check and isn't handed to anyone else.
If no open codes are left, staff can see the flagged code in the license list and replace it.

title: Choosing no kit clears kit gear
summary: When a reservation auto-picks a kit and you switch it to None, the kit's gear no longer stays selected on the next step.
details: Choosing None removes only the gear the kit added; anything you picked yourself stays.
Switching to a different kit swaps the gear the same way.
Fixed on the web and in the iOS app.

title: iPhone 1.3 fixes and What's new
summary: Staff links open in the iPhone app, past announcements have a home under Browse, dismissed announcements stay dismissed offline, and pickup desks come from the server.
details: Tapping a link to someone's staff page opens their profile in the app instead of an empty screen. Older web addresses keep working too.
Browse has a new What's new row that lists every app announcement you were shown, so you can reopen one after closing the splash.
Closing an announcement with no signal no longer brings it back on the next open. The app remembers and tells the server when it can.
The reservation pickup desk list now follows the server's list instead of names built into the app.
This is part of the next iPhone update on TestFlight.

title: Screenshots and guides for every app
summary: Every app in the directory now has a page with screenshots, features and workflow steps. Released apps show current download details, while apps in development are clearly labeled.
details: Fetch shows the 1.5.4 opening window, download preview, conversion preview and finished results.
Offload explains verified copying and the archive handoff using its public 1.5.3 interface.
Wisconsin Creative uses published App Store images, and Radio Clip and Media Lab show sample-data development previews.
All five listings link to their detail pages, with full-size screenshots and layouts for desktop and phone.

title: Email logo fix, emails opt-in
summary: The logo in our emails now loads in Outlook, and notification emails are off unless you turn them on.
details: Invites and password resets are always emailed.
To get schedule, gear, and trade emails, turn Email on in Settings > Notifications.

title: Keep non-game titles when adding an event
summary: Adding a visit or other non-game now points you to Non-game, so the title stays as you typed it instead of showing as Sport vs Opponent.
details: If a Home, Away, or Neutral event has a title without vs or at, Add event offers a one-tap switch to Non-game.
Game events still read as sport, vs or at, and opponent.

title: Less repeated work across devices
summary: The web and iPhone apps do less repeated loading and background work while keeping gear counts, schedules, and unfinished work current.
details: Home and navigation share count updates, and opening the app no longer rebuilds the page during saved-data restoration.
Unused searches leave memory sooner, while saved dashboard and booking details remain available.
Hidden web pages pause schedule refreshes and resume safely when you return.
Schedule, Resources, Sports settings, and hiring pages download less code on their first visit.
The iPhone app prepares list responses and brand previews away from interface updates, avoids duplicate saves, and skips return checks that are too early to be useful.

title: Out-of-town scoreboard has its own site
summary: The World Series out-of-town scoreboard, chip, router output and controller now live at ots.wisconsincreative.com, and old wisconsincreative.com/ots links redirect there.
details: Changes to the board go live in seconds instead of waiting on a full site deploy.
The controller now uses its own password instead of a staff sign-in.

title: World Series chip and router output
summary: A compact World Series score chip for the corner of the Camp Randall main videoboard, plus a 1920×1080 output that carries both scoreboards over HDMI for the video router.
details: The chip shows both teams' logos and scores, the inning and the outs, and follows the same controller as the fascia board.
wisconsincreative.com/ots/output puts the fascia board and the chip at exact pixel size on one full-HD frame, so a laptop can feed them straight into the router with no scaling.

title: Controller for the out-of-town scoreboard
summary: Staff can switch the Camp Randall out-of-town scoreboard between live, a demo and a frozen frame from wisconsincreative.com/ots/control, on any device.
details: Live follows the MLB game feed, and can be pointed at a different game.
Demo plays a sample scenario, like a walk-off or a grand slam, for testing on the board.
Hold freezes whatever is on screen.
The board picks up a change within about five seconds without reloading, and runs live if nothing is set.

title: Schedule notices read properly again
summary: The "Schedule changes" notice on an event's crew no longer squeezes its message into a narrow column.
details: Messages in notices with an icon and a title now use the full width.
Other notices of the same shape are fixed too.

title: World Series out-of-town scoreboard
summary: A live scoreboard for World Series Game 2 at wisconsincreative.com/ots, built for the out-of-town strip on Camp Randall's south end zone fascia.
details: Shows each team's city, logo and score, the inning, bases, count and outs, updating every few seconds from MLB's live feed.
Switches on its own between pregame, live innings, inning breaks and the final.
Plays on the board through Daktronics web page playback and keeps the last good score if the feed drops.

title: Position labels on event crew
summary: Staff can now tag each person on an event's crew with a position label, like SLOW1, and say which half they cover.
details: Add a label and choose Full game, 1st half, or 2nd half from the crew editor.
The tag shows next to the name on the Schedule list and the event page, including for students, and on the iPhone event crew.
Labels go out with the rest of the schedule and don't send a new notification by themselves.
Replacing someone clears the label for that spot.

title: Faster audit and resources pages
summary: The audit report and Resources pages now load noticeably faster, especially on a slow connection.
details: The audit report no longer downloads code it never uses, about a third less than before.
Resources only loads the file uploader when you start an upload.
Brand fonts are now kept on your device for a month instead of being rechecked each visit.

title: Announcements on iPhone
summary: Announcements posted from Settings now also appear in the iPhone app as a sheet the first time you open it.
details: Banner or swipeable images, a short message, and an optional button.
Closing it in any way marks it as seen, and the next one appears if more are waiting.
It checks when the app opens or returns to the foreground, never in the background.

title: Budget imports from the department workbook
summary: Admins can import a budget straight from the department spreadsheet, one tab at a time, and check it before anything is saved.
details: Pick the tab; the one for the budget's year (and Football) is suggested.
Statuses, supplier, price, budget, spent and month are read from the sheet's own columns.
Bought rows with no budget come in as Unplanned, and Dropped rows stay Dropped.
Running it again updates lines instead of adding copies.

title: Emails have a new look
summary: Every email from the app now uses the same Wisconsin Creative design, with the logo, one clear button, and a plain-text version.
details: Invites, password resets, shift trades, and reminders all share the new layout.
Overdue gear and damage reports use a red label so they stand out.
Replies can go to a staff inbox once one is set up.

title: Hiring invites are emailed
summary: New students now get an email with a sign-in link when you invite them, and you can resend it from Onboarding.
details: The link opens the login page with the invited address already filled in.
If email is not set up or a send fails, the invite is still created and the page tells you so.
Resend is limited to three per person per hour.

title: Booking activity on iPhone
summary: A reservation or checkout on iPhone shows what changed, including gear that was added or removed. Collaborators do not see this history.
details: Open Activity on a reservation or checkout to read the same history as the website.
Filter the list to booking changes or equipment changes.
A failed refresh keeps the history already on screen.
The newest 50 entries are shown. Older history stays on the website.
Collaborators do not see Activity.

title: Staff on iPhone
summary: The iPhone app now calls the people directory Staff and lets you filter it by role with one tap.
details: Users is now Staff in the tab bar and Browse.
Role tabs show how many students, staff, and admins there are.
The role option in the filter menu is gone, since the tabs replace it.

title: In-app announcements
summary: Quick news now appears as a short message the next time you open the app, so new features and updates reach everyone without waiting on a release.
details: Read it once, then it is gone for you.
Some come with pictures you can swipe through.
Some messages have a button that takes you straight to the new feature.
Admins write and publish them from Settings, no release needed.

title: Hours on your profile
summary: Your profile on iPhone shows the hours you worked this week and this month, using the same Monday-to-Sunday count as the website.
details: Open your profile to see this week and this month, with the number of shifts in each.
The week runs Monday through Sunday, Central time, including a Sunday evening shift.
If hours fail to load, the rest of your profile stays up and Try again is available.
A later refresh that fails keeps the hours already on screen.
Collaborators do not see hours.

title: Safer kiosk scans
summary: A second scan at the kiosk no longer creates another custody record, and due today follows the Chicago day.
details: Scanning an item that was already picked up or returned does not create a second custody record.
Returning a counted quantity that was already returned does not count it twice.
Due today, day chips, and night hours follow the Chicago day.
If a scan response is lost, the pickup or return list reloads from the server.
Staff need a staff card to add, remove, or swap gear on someone else's checkout.

title: Kit return time on iPhone
summary: A collaborator sees when a kit item comes back, even when the holder's name is hidden.
details: Open a kit and read Back plus the return time when the name is hidden.
Staff and admin still see With the name and the return time.
A hold with no return time stays unnamed.

title: Clearer status and recovery
summary: Reservations, checkouts, items, schedule, and kiosk stay understandable from the keyboard, and a failed list says so instead of looking empty.
details: Calendar and week events name home, away, or neutral in the control, not only by color.
A failed schedule, reservation check, parent search, gap count, or attachment search offers Try again.
Closing a confirmation, retire prompt, or kiosk activation dialog returns focus to the control that opened it.
Row menus, favorites, filters, and the item-type toggle keep the keyboard instead of paging or opening the row.

title: Item activity on iPhone
summary: Staff can read an item's history on iPhone, filtered to all activity, item updates, or bookings.
details: Open Activity on an item to see who changed it and when.
Filter to all activity, item updates, or bookings, and load older pages.
A booking row opens that booking.
A failed refresh keeps the history already on screen.
Students and collaborators do not see Activity. Previous bookings stay on the item.

title: Budget, kits and students for UA gear
summary: Admins see the Under Armour budget, what the department covers for each person, and a student list with sizes on the gear results.
details: Edit the total budget and student kit price, and mark it confirmed. Until then it carries a Placeholder tag. The budget and totals are visible to admins only.
Record the order the Equipment department places (PO, order number, dates), check gear in as it arrives, and mark pieces handed out person by person.
An Order table rolls staff kits, student kits and picks up into one quantity per item and size. Student shoes join once their style is chosen.
Each person shows Standard issue (covered by the department), Core kit where their fit has one, and the number of pieces they picked.
Add students to the list, see who is missing a top or shoe size, and fill sizes in for them. Sizes are saved to the student's profile.

Tabs for Overview, People, Order, Receiving, Handout and History keep the page easy to follow, and a Needs attention list shows what to fix next. History opens last year with its budget, items and people, and Save this year to History keeps a read-only copy of the current year.

title: Checkout days and kit privacy
summary: The checkout activity chart keeps every Madison day when the clocks change. A collaborator opening a kit no longer sees who currently has each piece.
details: Checkout activity includes the Madison day the clocks spring forward, and does not repeat the day they fall back.
A collaborator can still see whether a kit item is out and when that hold ends.
The person's name and the booking title stay off the collaborator kit response.
Staff and admin kit detail still names who has the gear.

title: Away game travel list
summary: An away game on iPhone lists who is traveling. Adding or removing someone stays on the website.
details: Open an away game in Schedule to see who is traveling.
Each person shows their name and area. Tap a person to open their profile.
A failed refresh keeps the travelers already on screen.
Home games do not show a travel section.
Adding and removing travelers stays on the website.

title: A fresher Staff section
summary: Staff, Workforce, Hiring and Onboarding have a new look, and Staff now shows who is working today.
details: Lato type, a calm blue accent, softer cards, and a colored dot for each area.
The org chart is a real chart with cards and connectors, plus a Not placed yet section.
Profiles get Email and Call buttons, an area chip, and an At a glance card.
Roster rows show an area dot and a Graduating chip, and hide the role column when a role tab already says it.
The roster shows an On shift now strip, and a new Today tab lists who is working which event now, later, and tomorrow.

Hiring and Onboarding Status get the same look: a targets strip, calmer board cards, one onboarding list, and an application sheet with a progress track, average rating, Watch interview card, and Pass and Hire buttons that stay in view.

title: Clearer, more reliable iPhone workflows
summary: The iPhone app groups secondary tools in Browse and makes gear choices easier to review. Schedule is now the single destination for events.
details: Browse groups tools into Work, Equipment, Resources, and Team, with Events removed in favor of Schedule.
UA Gear uses catalog size pickers on item and review screens, with separate controls for quantity, color, and size.
Gear drafts and reservation edits recover more reliably when loading or saving fails.
Accountability, Kits, Reports, Brand assets, Badges, Blasts, and Battery Ops have clearer layouts and improved large-text support.
Offline status leaves navigation buttons accessible, and inventory details load when first opened.
Reports keep pagination consistent, and Brand assets opens the file version shown in the list.

title: Condition reports on iPhone
summary: Staff can read damage and missing-item reports on an item, including the photo and the checkout they came from. Clearing maintenance stays in the item menu.
details: Open an item to see the five most recent condition reports, the same record as the website.
Damage is marked in orange and a missing item in red.
A photo opens full screen, and the checkout row opens that checkout.
Reports stay after maintenance is cleared. Students do not see this record.

title: Shared logins on iPhone
summary: Staff, students, and collaborators can copy a department login from the iPhone. Adding and archiving those logins stays on the website.
details: Browse includes Shared logins next to Photo Mechanic licenses.
Each login shows the account email. The password stays hidden until you show or copy it.
A shown password hides again after 30 seconds, and a copied password stays on this iPhone for 2 minutes.
Collaborators see the row only when shared software access is turned on.
Creating, editing, and archiving logins stays on the website.

title: Fetch and Offload app pages
summary: Fetch and Offload each have a dedicated page with features, Mac requirements, and download links. Open either page from Learn more on its app card.
details: See what each app does and how to get started before downloading it.
Find the Mac requirements, version, and download link together on each page.
Use Learn more on the Fetch and Offload cards to open their product pages.

title: Madison hours, charts, and exports
summary: Profile hours, staffing workload, item insight charts, and the default schedule export follow the Madison day. Catalog attachments stay with the items a collaborator can open.
details: Profile hours and staffing suggestions count the Madison week and month, including Sunday evening and a week that crosses the month.
Item insight charts file an evening checkout on the Madison day.
A schedule export with no end date includes an evening event on the last day.
The calendar source list is limited to people who can view sources.
A collaborator who can browse the catalog sees an item's attachments, without serial numbers.
Filling open shifts and copying a previous crew read each person once for the whole preview.

title: Safer due dates and scans
summary: Due today follows the Madison day. Pickup scans stay with the person at the kiosk, and scan codes stay on the checkouts people are allowed to see.
details: Due today on checkouts, reservations, and the combined list uses the Madison day, including the evening before midnight.
A start date range stays inside the reservation due-today queue.
A personal pickup scan has to be the requester or a staff member at the kiosk.
Checkout scan progress, including item codes, is limited to people who can view that checkout.
Item family units and products use the same catalog permission as the family.

title: Team badges on iPhone
summary: Staff can read the badge catalog on iPhone. Awarding a group of people still happens on the website.
details: Browse includes Badges for staff and admins.
The list shows the manual badges that can be awarded, with the same names and descriptions as the website.
View report opens the existing read-only badge report.
Awarding a badge to several people stays on the website.

title: Faster search and item lists
summary: Searching the catalog and opening item families reads less from the database, and the family photo control shows when it has keyboard focus.
details: Command search and scans skip the six catalog-wide status counts the Items page still uses.
Item families count units in the database instead of loading every unit onto the list.
Guide search still finds a word split across a markdown link, and skips bodies that cannot contain the phrase.
Print Labels reads every alphabetical page and skips the catalog status counts.
The item-family photo button shows its Edit label and a focus ring from the keyboard.

title: UA gear picks on iPhone
summary: People on this year's Under Armour list can choose their gear on iPhone, up to their allowance, and submit it.
details: Browse includes UA Gear for students, staff, and admins.
The list is the fit you were given, with prices and sizes from this year's catalog.
Save a draft or submit. You can still change a submitted list until the deadline.
After the deadline the saved list stays visible and locked.
The roster, deadline, and equipment spreadsheet stay on the web.

title: Brand assets on iPhone
summary: The iPhone app can open logos and PDFs from Brand assets. Adding files stays on the web.
details: Browse includes Brand assets for anyone who can read Resources.
Open a folder, or search the library by name.
A logo or PDF opens on the phone. Other files can be shared to another app.
Adding folders, uploading, and restoring an older version stay on the web.

title: Late returns on iPhone
summary: Students and staff can open the late-return list on iPhone and go from a person to the checkout.
details: Browse includes Accountability for students, staff, and admins.
The list covers this academic year or all time, sorted by late returns, late time, or most recent.
Your own place on the list stays at the top. Search looks through the names already loaded.
A person shows each late checkout, and opening one shows the gear.
Spreadsheets and taking a checkout off the list stay on the website.

title: Edit reservations on iPhone
summary: Reservations on iPhone can be updated the same way as on the web. Checkout screens also pick up the extra actions staff already have there.
details: Change a reservation's name, notes, pickup, dates, remaining gear, and linked events.
Save waits until that gear is available for the new window.
Gear that was already picked up stays on the checkout.
Checkouts can nudge, close without a scan, transfer, or switch between shared and personal when those actions are allowed.
Extend stays the main action on a checkout. Gear on an active checkout still changes at a kiosk.

title: Kits and batteries on iPhone
summary: Staff and students can read kits and item families on iPhone. Staff can also open Battery Ops to see what is low and who has batteries out.
details: Kits show whether the gear is ready, who has something out, and when it is due.
Item families show how many are available and which units are checked out.
Battery Ops lists low camera pairings and the batteries that are out.
Reserve is the action on a kit or family. Editing, receiving, labels, and repairs stay on the web.

title: Faster lists and reports
summary: Items, Battery Ops, and condition flags read less from the database, and several staff pages show their own loading state while they open.
details: Most popular still ranks the same way, and it totals recent use in the database instead of loading every booking and scan.
Battery Ops looks at battery-like families and camera-like gear first, then keeps the same families as before.
Scan history, open unit checkouts, and recent condition flags show up faster.
Reports, Settings, Resources, UA staff gear, signatures, YouTube, Blasts, Operations, Scoreboard, and Software show a page skeleton while they load.
Add item, Fill gaps, and Cleanup load separately from the Items list.

title: Budget tracking for admins
summary: Admins can now track planned and actual spending by fiscal year on a new Budget page, with separate budgets for Creative and Football. Staff and admins also get a Wish list.
details: Create a budget for a fiscal year, add lines with category, supplier, quantity, and cost, and record the PO and order numbers once something is bought.

See spent, planned but not bought, and remaining at a glance, with an Insights view of spend by month, suppliers, and year over year, and a CSV download. Dropped lines stay in the fixed submitted plan, and lines added later are marked Unplanned.
Fiscal years read as FY26 · Jul 2025 – Jun 2026, matching the July 1 start.

Link a purchase to the items it bought, with suggested matches, and fill an item's purchase details from the order without overwriting anything already there. Every line keeps a history, refunds and credits count against its cost, and you can drop or recategorize many lines at once with an undo.
A new Wish list lets staff and admins paste a link or type what they need. Admins approve, decline, or move a wish into the budget as a line, and past years can be imported from a spreadsheet.
Only admins can see or change the budget, and every change is logged.

title: Full reports on iPhone
summary: Staff can open the rest of the reports from the iPhone Reports screen. Spreadsheets still download on the web.
details: Utilization, Checkouts, Scans, Missing Units, and Badges are read-only on the phone.
Checkouts and utilization keep a simple chart for the period you pick.
Scans can be limited to checkout or check-in, and Missing Units can be limited to a location or category.
Usage appears only for the account allowed to see those counts.
CSV downloads stay on the web.

title: Redesigned Photo Mechanic licenses
summary: Getting a Photo Mechanic license is now one button, and staff manage codes from a compact list.
details: Students claim with one button; the best open slot is picked and the code is copied.
A new list shows who is using Photo Mechanic right now.
Your license is a large card with a tap-to-copy code, expiry, and return.
Staff get a compact list of codes with both slots at a glance, plus filters for open, full, and expiring codes.

title: Blasts stay after you dismiss them
summary: The phone keeps blasts you have already seen, and a kiosk handoff no longer crashes when the saved request is incomplete.
details: Browse has a Blasts list and a detail screen for broadcasts you have opened on this phone.
Got it still clears the home banner. The message stays in Blasts so you can read it again.
A blast this phone has never fetched is not in that list.
Kiosk checkout and pickup retries report an error instead of crashing when the handoff request has no address or body.

title: Events in the iOS app
summary: The iOS app can browse events, including linked gear and bookings, from the same calendar the website uses.
details: Browse includes Events for anyone who can see the calendar.
The list shows what is coming up, or the past 30 days.
An event shows when it is, where it is, who it came from, and the bookings and gear linked to it.
Open in Schedule shows the crew and call times that were already on Schedule.
Creating or editing an event stays on the website.

title: Clearer Workforce overview
summary: The Workforce overview now shows, area by area, who stays and who graduates, so gaps are visible before they happen.
details: A new Coverage by area list shows each area's full-time staff and how many students stay or graduate.
Areas that lose half or more of their students, or all of them, are flagged and listed first.
The top tiles add context, such as the share of students graduating.
Select an area in the list to jump to its people.

title: Cleaner Staff roster
summary: The Staff page now filters by role with one tap, and you can switch the roster between a table and a photo grid.
details: Role tabs at the top show how many students, staff, admins, and collaborators match your search and filters.
The role dropdown and the separate breakdown cards are gone, so there is one place to look.
A new photo grid view shows everyone as headshot cards. Your choice stays in the page link.
Group by area splits the whole list under Photo, Video, and the other areas, with each area's full headcount, even across pages.
Hover a name in the table to see a quick card with title, location, and contact details.
Year and sport filters only appear when they apply to students.

title: Workforce moves under Staff
summary: Workforce is now a tab on the Staff page instead of its own menu item. It is still visible to admins only.
details: Admins see Roster and Workforce tabs at the top of Staff.
Hiring and Planning sit inside the Workforce tab.
Old Workforce links redirect to the new location.

title: Users is now Staff
summary: The Users page and menu item are now called Staff. Old Users links and bookmarks still take you to the right place.
details: The sidebar, page title, search results, and breadcrumbs say Staff.
Profile links now live under /staff, and old /users links redirect automatically.
Nothing about who can see the page or what it shows has changed.

title: Lighter pages on the web
summary: Heavy screens download less JavaScript before they can be used. The pages themselves look the same.
details: The overdue report loads its chart only when that chart is needed, the same way the other reports do.
Schedule week and calendar views load when you switch to them.
Date fields load the calendar grid separately from the rest of the page.
Public about pages and several staff screens open with a smaller first download.

title: Live updates pause overnight
summary: Booking, inventory, and audit live updates pause from 10 PM to 6 AM Central, then pick up again in the morning.
details: Open booking and inventory pages stop asking for changes overnight and refresh on their own after 6 AM.
Audit auto-refresh follows the same overnight pause.
Badge celebrations wait until morning instead of checking through the night.
Bringing a tab back during the day still refreshes right away.

title: Photo Frame for showcasing photos
summary: Drop in a photo and get a clean, modern frame with its camera settings and photographer credit, ready to post.
details: Reads camera, lens, focal length, aperture, shutter speed and ISO from the photo itself, and every field can be edited or switched off.
Sized for social by default: 4:5, with 1:1, 9:16 and Original as options. Frames are black, with preset colors and a color picker.
Exports a PNG, 2160 px wide for the social sizes or the photo's full resolution for Original. The photo never leaves your browser.

title: Uniform app cards on the apps page
summary: Every app on the apps page now has the same card layout, with the Wisconsin Creative screenshot removed.
details: Each card shows the app icon, name, badges, description, version and requirement, and the download link in the same places.
Cards line up in rows of three on a wide screen, two on a tablet and one on a phone.

title: Board Sizes layout restored with Copy spec
summary: Board Sizes has its top venue bar and dotted background back, and keeps the new Copy spec buttons.
details: Venues are tabs across the top again, and Content types and Game day are no longer in the navigation.
Copy spec, the More menu and the clearer dark colors from the last update stay.

title: Copy a board's exact size
summary: Board Sizes lists every venue board so you can find one and copy its pixel size, aspect ratio, and any safe area already on file.
details: Search across Camp Randall, the Kohl Center, the Field House, LaBahn, and Goodman, then narrow to one venue or to open questions.
Copy spec puts the size, aspect ratio, position, and recorded safe area on the clipboard.
Guide SVG and Guide PNG download at that board's exact pixel size.
Open questions stay on the board, including Kohl Center frame rates and the unconfirmed Goodman board.

title: Fetch on the apps page
summary: The apps page now lists Fetch, a Mac app that saves videos and audio from a link, with a download button.
details: Fetch saves video as an MP4 that plays everywhere, or audio only, from YouTube, Instagram, X, podcasts and more.
The card shows the current version and requires macOS 27 or later.
All app icons on the page now appear at the same size.

title: Apps and tools page
summary: wisconsincreative.com/apps now lists the team's apps and tools in one place.
details: Apps: the Wisconsin Creative iPhone and iPad app, Offload, and Radio Clip (coming soon), with current versions and release dates.
Tools: Golden Hour, Timelapse, Board Sizes, and QR Studio.
Light and dark appearance, following your system by default, with a picker at the top.
The page opens without signing in.

title: Sourced apps page facts
summary: The apps page now uses the published App Store and Offload release facts, including the home screenshot, and opens without signing in.
details: Wisconsin Creative shows its App Store version, the iOS it requires, and the home screenshot.
Offload shows version 1.2.0, macOS 15.0 or later, and that version's download.
Radio Clip no longer shows a version that was never published.
The page opens without signing in. It is still left out of search.

title: Request shifts before release
summary: Students can now request an open Student shift as soon as it exists, without waiting for staff to release the crew.
details: The Claim shift button shows on open Student slots on Event detail and in the Schedule list.
Requests still go to an Admin for approval, and you can withdraw one while it waits.
Staff edits in progress still pause requests until they are released.

title: Gear bookings no longer assign shifts
summary: Booking gear for an event no longer puts you on that event's schedule, and staff can remove people a booking added earlier.
details: Linking a reservation to an event only attaches the gear to the event.
If you are already scheduled for the event, the booking still links to your slot.
Staff can now unassign someone a past gear booking placed on the schedule; the booking keeps its gear and event.

title: Faster Operations page
summary: Operations shows each check lane as soon as it loads, and Import’s wizard steps are clearer.
details: Operations no longer waits for every queue before showing anything — ready lanes appear first, with the rest filling in.
If Operations cannot load at all, you get a clear retry instead of a blank page.
Import’s step rail and header explain the CSV → map → preview → import path with larger step targets.

title: Clearer first-day setup
summary: New accounts set up their profile on the Welcome page itself, and Blasts recover cleanly when a load fails.
details: After you create your account, Welcome walks through contact, Wiscard, and other details on the page instead of opening a separate dialog over a status card.
On a wider screen, a step list shows what is done and what is next. You can still continue later from Home.
Invited sign-in copy explains that a short welcome setup follows password creation.
If blasts or welcome setup cannot load, you get a clear retry instead of an empty or stuck screen.

title: Hiring board recovers
summary: Hiring keeps the applicant board when a refresh fails and gives a clear Retry instead of a dead end.
details: If Hiring cannot load cycles or applicants, you get Retry instead of a stuck empty page.
A failed refresh keeps the last loaded board for that cycle so work is not wiped.
Search and filters that hide every applicant offer Clear filters.

title: Blasts load recovery
summary: Blast history and welcome setup recover cleanly when the network fails, and blast detail is easier to scan.
details: If blasts cannot load, you get a clear retry instead of an empty list that looks like nothing was ever sent.
Blast detail separates a missing blast from a failed load, refreshes on demand, and stacks recipients as cards on smaller screens.
Compose shows a retry when events or people cannot be loaded for targeting.
Welcome setup no longer stays on a loading screen forever when profile completion fails.

title: YouTube queue recovers
summary: YouTube Studio Lite’s review queue offers clear next steps when the library is empty, a refresh fails, or filters hide every upload.
details: An empty library shows Refresh library when the channel can be checked.
A failed refresh keeps the error visible with Retry refresh.
Filters that hide every upload offer Clear filters.

title: Reservations keep kit custody
summary: Calling a gameday kit on a reservation keeps the real status, so a checked-out camera is not labeled available.
details: The kit loaded into the reservation includes who has each piece and when that hold ends.
Every piece in the kit is still added for review.

title: Clearer Settings and account deletion
summary: Settings pages are easier to find and jump between, collaborator access warns before you leave unsaved changes, and you can delete your account from web Security.
details: Settings names and related links now match what you see in the Settings menu, including clearer paths for calendar and overdue rules.
Collaborator access shows unsaved changes, lets you reset, and warns if you leave mid-edit.
On the web, Security now includes Delete account with the same password confirmation and retention rules as the iPhone app.

title: Kits list shows gear that's out
summary: The kits list no longer calls a kit Ready when some of its cameras are checked out, pending pickup, in maintenance, or retired.
details: A kit with some serialized pieces unavailable says how many are out.
A kit whose serialized pieces are all unavailable says Out.
Item families stay in the contents count and do not change that badge.

title: Schedule day headers stay put
summary: Schedule list day headers stay directly under the filter bar after you change filters, so the first rows of a day stay visible.
details: Changing or clearing filters no longer leaves a blank gap under Load older records.
A day header no longer sticks mid-page and hides the first event of that day.

title: Kit page shows who has gear
summary: A kit page now says when a camera is checked out or waiting for pickup, and names the person who has it.
details: Checked-out and pending-pickup pieces no longer look available just because they are still marked on the shelf.
Maintenance and retired pieces keep those labels.
The kiosk kit checklist receives the same status and name.

title: Add items before pickup
summary: Reservations waiting at the kiosk have an Add items button, on the booking page and on the kiosk pickup screen.
details: It opens equipment editing right away, with the same availability checks as before.
At the kiosk, scanning a battery or counted bin that is not on the reservation now offers Add instead of an error.
Items already picked up stay on their checkout.

title: Reserve gear that is out
summary: On iPhone, reservation search includes cameras and lenses that are checked out, as long as pickup starts after they come back.
details: Search and browse show checked-out, pending-pickup, and reserved gear, not only what is on the shelf.
You can add it when pickup is at least an hour after the current hold ends. A tighter handoff stays blocked and says who has it.
Scanning a barcode follows the same rule.

title: Shared case pickup works from home
summary: Tapping a shared case under Ready for pickup or Coming up on the kiosk now asks who is picking it up, instead of doing nothing.
details: Pick yourself from the roster and the pickup starts as you.
The log shows who handed the case over, not whoever reserved it.
Works even when the person who reserved the case is not on the kiosk roster.
A shared case for a later day, like an away game, can be picked up early.

title: Schedule list rows line up
summary: Schedule list rows stay lined up with the header when an event has no crew yet.
details: Events with no shifts no longer shift status and actions one column to the left.
The list fades in, and the loading placeholder matches the shape of a row.

title: Move a signature to the right person
summary: A signature saved on the wrong roster spot can be moved to the right person, and the signer's name shows on the line before you save.
details: The capture screen shows the person's name and number on the signature line so a wrong slot is obvious before Save.
Move signature to… sends the saved signature and its history to a blank person. Creative Staff signatures stay put.
Team rosters can add an unofficial player, marked Unofficial, until the official roster includes them.
Applying an official roster keeps staff-added players and adopts them when the same name appears officially.

title: Badge celebrations check less often
summary: The iOS app stops checking for new badges while it sits open, which keeps our servers asleep overnight.
details: Badge celebrations still show right away when you open or return to the app.
A phone left open on a desk no longer checks for badges all night.
A badge someone else awards you while the app is already open appears the next time you open it.

title: No Claim on unreleased crews
summary: Students no longer see a Claim button on shifts staff haven't released yet.
details: Open shifts on a crew that hasn't been released now say claims open once it is released, instead of failing with a draft error.
Once staff release the crew, the Claim buttons appear as usual.

title: Stay signed in
summary: You stay signed in while you keep using the app, and a password sign-in can quietly become a passkey.
details: Using the app keeps your sign-in alive. A remembered sign-in lasts as long as you return at least once every 30 days.
"Keep me signed in" now starts ticked and also appears when you create your account. Untick it on a shared computer.
After signing in, you land back on the page you were trying to open.
After a password sign-in, your password manager can save a passkey for next time without asking.
The Mac app can fill in the password you saved for the website.

title: Mac app status and shortcuts
summary: The GearOps menu bar app tells you when its numbers might be out of date and is quicker to use from the keyboard.
details: Data that hasn't been confirmed for 15 minutes is marked Needs attention.
Opening the menu refreshes it, at most once a minute.
Search bookings, move through rows with the arrow keys, and choose to count only overdue items.
Control-Option-Command-G opens a Status window when macOS hides the menu bar icon.

title: Dismiss damage flags
summary: Staff can clear a handled damage flag from the dashboard, and an item's page now shows its recent condition reports.
details: Each flagged item appears once on the dashboard, most serious first.
Click a damaged or lost item to review the report and photo, as before.
The × beside a damage flag hides it from the dashboard; the report stays in the item's history.
Item Info lists the five most recent condition reports with their photos.

title: Accurate notification badge
summary: The iPhone app's badge now matches your unread notifications.
details: Tapping a notification marks it read.
The app icon badge updates to your real unread count instead of a stale number.

title: Equipment sheet export
summary: Organizers can download the equipment department's order sheet already filled from everyone's submitted gear picks, instead of copying a CSV into it by hand.
details: Each item and color gets one row, with counts by size, in the department's own sheet.
Shoes, sideline gear and headwear, and team catalog items land in their matching sections.
Sizes the sheet has no column for, like pant waists and fitted caps, are listed in the notes.
Totals and the remaining budget calculate when the sheet opens.

title: Release notes
summary: A public Releases page lists what shipped and when across web, iOS, the kiosk, and the Mac app, going back to the first build.
details: The page opens on the last eight weeks, with earlier history one click away.
Filter by app (Web, iOS, Kiosk, Mac) or by new features, improvements, and fixes.
Weekly fix roundups fold into one line you can expand.
Follow along with the RSS feed.
Every future update adds its own entry here.

title: Gear picks free-kit heads-up
summary: Gear picks now point out when something you're adding is already in your free kit, and colors appear in a consistent order.
details: Adding the first pick of a style that's already in your standard issue or core kit shows a short heads-up naming the kit color.
It never blocks you: Add to picks keeps going, and it asks only once per style.
Every item lists Red, then White, then Black before other colors, on cards, swatches, previews, and the review sheet.

title: Staff gear picks
summary: Staff can choose their 2027-28 apparel and equipment in the app within their allowance, then review and submit, while organizers see everyone's picks in one place.
details: A catalog with an allowance bar shows what you've picked and what's left as you go.
Review lets you change size, quantity, and color inline, and sizes default from your profile.
A short How it works intro appears on your first visit and can be reopened from the header.
Your picks are kept if a save or reload fails, and Show all gear clears filters when nothing matches.
Organizers see results and can export them as a CSV.

title: Item cleanup wizard
summary: A guided wizard walks staff through items one at a time to fill gaps in inventory records, so labels, serials, and accessories are accurate before they're needed.
details: Confirm or fill in each item's QR label and serial number.
Attach cages, plates, and grips to the camera they belong to.

title: Damage report review
summary: Damage reports filed at the kiosk now land on the dashboard, where staff can see the photo and send the item to maintenance in one step.
details: Each report opens a review panel with the photo, the reporter's notes, and a link to the item.
Reports can cover numbered batteries and counted supplies, not just individually tracked gear.

title: Kiosk stops auto-selecting kits
summary: Kiosk checkout no longer picks a suggested kit for you; you choose a kit only when you want one.
details: The suggested kit is still highlighted in the kit picker so it's easy to find.
Choosing a kit uses it as your checklist while you scan gear.

title: YouTube metadata tool
summary: Admins can connect the program's YouTube channel and keep video titles, descriptions, and playlists consistent from inside the app.
details: A YouTube page connects or disconnects the team channel.
A review queue lists the last 30 days of videos with suggested titles and descriptions.
Editors save a draft per video, then review and publish titles, descriptions, and playlists.
Naming rules guide the suggestions so uploads follow one house style.

title: Fixes and polish
summary: Kit, kiosk, and calendar fixes from the week after the kiosk redesign.
details: Football travel kits can share cameras with game-day kits, and kit pages find batteries again.
Kiosk no longer offers to change items on a pending pickup where that isn't possible.
Today and Tomorrow sections on a kiosk left running overnight now roll over at midnight.
Cleaned up many small kiosk layout, title, and wording issues.

title: Label print cart
summary: Staff can collect item labels in a print cart, review them, and export ready-to-print files, instead of printing labels one at a time.
details: Add labels to the cart from across the app and review them before printing.
Export a separate file for each label printer template.

title: iOS sign-in redesign
summary: The iPhone app's launch and sign-in screens get a cleaner dark design and calmer handling of offline and expired sessions, along with better date pickers.
details: An offline launch offers Try again, and an expired session shows a calm notice instead of an error.
Today, Tomorrow, and Now labels roll over at midnight if the app stays open overnight.
Subscribed shift calendars use full sport names, with promotion details moved to the event notes.

title: Workforce and student hiring
summary: Admins get a Workforce area that shows the whole staff and student picture and runs student hiring cycles from application to account invite.
details: An overview shows staff and students by area, with class standing, graduation, start terms, and sport assignments.
A Planning tab projects student headcount per area for coming years, including graduating, hired, and pipeline.
Hiring tracks applicants through Applied, Reviewed, Round 1, Hire, and Passed, with resumes, interview links, and notes.
Import applicants and roster history from spreadsheets, and upload many resumes matched by file name.
Marking someone Hire creates a prefilled student invitation that links to their account once they sign up.
Applicant personal details are removed automatically after the retention period for a closed cycle.

title: Calmer iPhone Home and Schedule
summary: iPhone Home and Schedule move to a flatter, calmer style that puts what's next first.
details: Home uses flat cards, number-first stats, and one Next Up list grouped into Overdue, Today, and Later.
A Schedule card on Home lists upcoming team events you aren't working, with near times like in 45 min.
Schedule, Trade Board, and event detail open at the current or next event.
Schedule remembers your filters, flags overlapping shifts, and lists trades and open slots together, soonest first.

title: Kiosk staff ID and pickup editing
summary: A round of kiosk follow-ups from live use on the iPad: staff actions now need a staff ID card, pickups can be edited, and battery problems can be reported.
details: Staff scan their staff ID card to change someone else's due time or transfer their checkout.
Change a pickup's title, event, and due time right at the kiosk.
Report a problem now covers numbered batteries and counted supplies, so a return can still finish.
Someone checking out for an event they aren't staffed on can request a crew spot for admin review.
Open an event from Events today to see its crew, their gear, and who still needs gear.
Checkout preselects your next shift, and booking sheets group gear by category with photos and tags.

title: Kiosk redesign
summary: The kiosk is rebuilt across home, person hub, checkout, pickup, and return, with clearer steps and new ways to hand off, undo, and report gear without finding a staff member.
details: Home groups overdue, due today, pickups, and game-day crews, with photos and the week's reservations when quiet.
Hand all or part of a checkout to anyone on the roster, or nudge an overdue holder once a day.
Undo a mistaken scan, swap a unit for the same model in one scan, and get a receipt after checkout.
Report gear as damaged, with an optional photo, or missing during a return; staff are notified.
Scans show when gear is next needed, play distinct sounds by result, and extensions show the latest possible return.
Larger system type, flat surfaces, a color per section, time presets, and a month calendar for return dates.

title: Football travel support
summary: Road trips are easier to staff and return from: travel gear can be returned by anyone at the kiosk, and default travelers are added in one step.
details: Anyone signed in at the kiosk can return items from another person's checkout as travel gear comes back.
Add defaults on an away game's Travel card puts every default traveler for that sport on the trip.
Default travelers can be turned off again, are listed first, and only people who can travel are offered.

title: Notification controls
summary: Notifications are easier to control and more dependable, with per-type levels, quiet hours, shift reminders, and alerts that group instead of piling up.
details: iOS: Set each notification type to Off, Silent, or Standard, set quiet hours, and pause until a chosen time.
You get a reminder two hours before a published shift with the event, area, and call time.
Alerts group by checkout or event, newer updates replace older ones, and wording says what to do next.
iOS: Lock-screen actions include Mark as Read, Remind Me in 1 Hour, and Approve or Decline for admins.
The app icon badge matches your unread count, and iOS Settings links straight to notification settings.
Delivery is tracked end to end, retries no longer send duplicates, and every type follows your settings.

title: Redesigned iOS Schedule
summary: The iPhone Schedule becomes one continuous list with a week strip, and the Trade Board and shift feed get a round of reliability fixes.
details: A swipeable week strip jumps through the list and expands into a month grid.
Quick filter chips and toolbar toggles for My Shifts and Sport, with your own work highlighted.
Opens instantly from your last view; pull down for earlier weeks, and every role can browse past events.
Open slots show how many student claims are waiting and link to the Trade Board.
Trade Board drops trades on cancelled events, keeps call times on approval, and reports results correctly.
The shift calendar feed shows only published crews, and its link sheet adds Share Link.

title: QR Studio
summary: A free public tool on the site makes branded, scan-checked QR codes, so anyone on the team can make a reliable code without third-party generators.
details: Make codes for links, Wi-Fi, email, phone, text messages, and contacts.
Each code is checked to scan correctly before you download it.

title: Guides in search and Resources handbook
summary: Guides are easier to find and read: they now show up in app-wide search, and Resources opens like a handbook.
details: Quick search and the Search page match guides by title, category, author, summary, and content.
Resources opens with a featured guide, guides grouped by type, jump chips, and a tools strip.
How-to guides support copyable paths and commands, screenshots between steps, and before/after images.
The guide editor adds a Callout menu and a Video button, and iOS renders guides like the web.

title: Web navigation, settings, and profiles
summary: The web app's sidebar, Settings, and profiles are reorganized so common destinations are easier to find.
details: The sidebar groups daily work, Team, Library, and Operations, and notifications move to a bell in the top bar.
Settings opens on a searchable directory, with Booking and Schedule settings grouped separately.
Profiles lead with role, title or year, and a Scoreboard link, with Info split into Contact, Work, and Assignments.
The team Scoreboard leads with the official record, and its filters are saved in a shareable link.

title: Schedule toolbar and activity
summary: The web Schedule is simpler to filter and browse, shows what changed recently, and gives staff more scheduling tools.
details: The toolbar has View, My Shifts, a searchable Sport filter, a Filters panel, and Clear.
A pinned activity strip shows recent assignments and calendar changes, with old and new values.
The list starts around today and loads older and newer events as you scroll.
Add event starts as a home game today and fills the title from sport and opponent.
Auto assign adds Scope and Review steps, and staff can add slots, publish now, and hold overlapping shifts.

title: iOS 27 look and New Reservation
summary: The iPhone app picks up the iOS 27 look and a cleaner way to build reservations.
details: Refined Liquid Glass styling with bars that recede while scrolling, while still supporting iOS 26.
Pickup and return share one row with a 15-minute time menu, and Review appears once gear is chosen.
Gear search sits in the navigation bar, rows swipe to add or remove, and unavailable gear is marked.
Review names who holds conflicting gear and uses a stepper for counted supplies.

title: Redesigned event page
summary: The event page is reorganized around crew, travel, and activity, with crew management and claim review happening right on each row.
details: Separate crew, travel, and activity cards, with crew fill in the header and a timeline of calendar changes.
Filled rows offer Replace and Unassign, and open rows offer Assign and Remove.
Pending claims and trades show as avatars on crew rows, with Approve and Decline for admins.
One form creates and edits events, and hand-added events can be hidden or deleted.
Ended events let staff record people who worked without a slot, without notifying anyone.

title: Game-day kits
summary: Kits bundle a camera package so anyone can reserve or check out a full game-day setup in one step on the web, iPhone, or kiosk.
details: Choosing a kit adds its cameras, lenses, and batteries to a reservation or checkout for review.
Football kits can be assigned game-day jobs, and pickers suggest the kit from your last game.
Kiosk checkout can start from a kit, showing its remaining items as a scan checklist.
Pickup lists a kit's actual items, empty kits are hidden, and each camera belongs to one kit per sport.

title: Re-reserve a past booking
summary: Start next week's reservation from a completed booking, with the person, pickup location, notes, and gear already filled in.
details: Works from completed checkouts and past reservations on the web and iPhone.
The copy is shifted to a new event of your choosing.

title: Flexible kiosk pickups
summary: Kiosk pickups now match what actually leaves the room: add or remove items, swap units, and pick up leftovers later on the same checkout.
details: Scan an extra item to add it to the reservation, or remove items you aren't taking.
