details: Closing requires a reason and confirmation that the gear is back.
Closing marks items returned and puts batteries and stock back into availability.
The kiosk remains the standard place to return gear.

title: Live booking updates
summary: The dashboard, bookings list, booking details, and Items pages now refresh on their own when something changes, so staff always see current gear status.
details: An indicator shows whether sync is live, paused, offline, or retrying.
Checkout list and detail pages show whether booking changes are up to date.
Item lists and detail pages update when someone else changes an item.

title: Dedicated kiosk app
summary: The kiosk now runs as its own iPad app that opens straight into kiosk mode, so check-in stations no longer depend on the main app.
details: Kiosk lists and the hub load reliably instead of showing up empty.
When something fails, the kiosk shows the real reason instead of always blaming the internet.
Typing on the kiosk keeps the normal keyboard, and controls respond reliably.

title: Edit active checkouts at the kiosk
summary: Staff can change an active checkout at the kiosk without starting over or going to the web.
details: Change a checkout's title or return time.
Scan in another item to add it to the checkout.
Remove items that haven't been returned yet.

title: Cleaner events and venue mapping
summary: Synced events get cleaner titles and more accurate home, away, and neutral labels, and each crew row shows one call time.
details: Event titles drop source prefixes, rankings, and school boilerplate, and venue spellings are cleaned up.
Each location's Home Venue setting decides whether a home-listed game is really home or neutral.
Admins can review venue mappings that are missing or point at inactive locations, with links to fix them.
Events can be marked Non-game, and the gear pickup location is set separately from the venue.
Crew rows, the assignment grid, and My Shifts show a single effective call time per person or slot.
Each person's Staff or Student scheduling class is set on their profile and drives labels and assignment.

title: Shift preferences and time off
summary: Students can tell staff when they prefer to work and request time off, so assignments account for more than class conflicts.
details: Students mark times they prefer or dislike working.
Time-off requests go to staff, who approve or deny them.

title: Smarter staffing tools
summary: Staff get ranked suggestions, an auto-fill preview, and work queues that point to exactly what still needs attention before an event.
details: The assign picker ranks people as Recommended, Good fit, Warning, or Overloaded, with short reasons.
Auto-fill previews proposed assignments, skipped slots, and warnings before anything changes.
Readiness cards and shareable work queues surface open slots, conflicts, pending requests, trades, and gear gaps.
Event pages compare a crew to the sport template and preview copying crew from the last matching event.
Schedule flags events missing a sport, opponent, or venue, and exports rosters, hours, and conflicts to CSV.
Events and assignments show whether gear is reserved, ready for pickup, or checked out.

title: Draft crews and publishing
summary: Crews can be built as drafts and published when ready, so workers only hear about changes once the schedule is final.
details: Staff publish a crew when it's ready, and assigned workers can acknowledge their shifts.
Draft changes don't notify anyone until published, and schedule and trade alerts open the related event.
Published open Student slots appear on the Trade Board alongside posted trades.
Event pages list recent crew, shift, publish, and gear changes, flagging ones made after publishing.
Notification settings add toggles for schedule, trade, and gear-prep alerts.

title: Reservation pickup at the kiosk
summary: Reservations that are due now show up on the kiosk as pickups, and scanning the gear turns the reservation into a checkout.
details: Due reservations appear on the kiosk; scan the gear and confirm to start the checkout.
A pickup that was started and left can be resumed with earlier scans already checked off.
Rows in Items Out, Active Checkouts, and Overdue open a detail view of who has the gear and when it's due.
A status dot shows connection health, with a Retry banner when a refresh fails.
If someone takes an item at the same moment, checkout shows a clear conflict message.

title: Kiosk checkout with Wiscard
summary: Students start at the kiosk by scanning their Wiscard, and every kiosk checkout now records what the gear is for and when it's coming back.
details: Scanning a Wiscard opens that person's kiosk hub, with the roster and a new A to Z filter as a fallback.
Checkouts ask for an upcoming event or a purpose, which becomes the booking title.
A return time picker checks scanned gear against other bookings and tight turnarounds before finishing.
Scanned gear shows photos, and numbered batteries, including older label formats, group into one row with unit chips.
Kiosk scans update each item's location and note when gear wasn't where expected.
Profiles hold a Wiscard number, admins can re-pair a kiosk iPad, and staff can test hand scanners on iOS.

title: Checkouts move to the kiosk
summary: Gear now changes hands only at the kiosk. The web and iOS apps create reservations and show checkouts and their history.
details: Starting a checkout, picking up a reservation, and returning gear happen at the kiosk only.
Item pages offer Reserve instead of Check out.
Missing-gear actions on an event reserve gear for the assigned worker instead of starting a checkout.
Event pages label crew gear, reservations, and missing gear consistently, and prompt you to set up a crew first.

title: Kiosk visual consistency
summary: Colors, buttons, and progress rings now match across every kiosk screen, with larger touch targets.
details: Progress rings run blue to green on every screen, and completion buttons use Wisconsin red.
Overdue is red everywhere, and pickups waiting on you are orange.
Back, camera, and remove-item buttons are large enough to tap easily.

title: iOS Schedule with multi-day events
summary: The iOS Schedule adopts the new card style and shows events that span several days.
details: Multi-day events appear on every day they cover with a Day n of m marker.
Event detail and date headers have a cleaner design.

title: iOS Liquid Glass redesign
summary: The iOS app moves to a shared card style with native Liquid Glass controls across its main screens.
details: Home, Bookings, Items, and detail screens share one card style.
Forms, Schedule, and Login adopt Liquid Glass controls.
Booking detail, the bookings list, and Home show real user photos.

title: Kiosk standby clock
summary: The kiosk stays awake as an always-on station, showing a live clock and today's events between sessions.
details: The kiosk stays signed in, its screen no longer sleeps, and the home screen shows a large live clock.
At night or when idle, it dims to a moving clock to protect the screen, and a tap wakes it.
Home lists today's and tomorrow's events with assigned crew, and tapping one shows event and call times.
Items Out, Active Checkouts, and Overdue stat cards open their matching lists with item photos.
Activation accepts a hardware keyboard and paste, and says when a code is too short or invalid.

title: Battery label export
summary: Staff can print numbered battery labels in bulk and keep track of which units already have one.
details: Export battery labels as a CSV for the label printer.
Mark which unit labels have been printed.

title: Scan result card on iOS
summary: Scanning a single item on iOS opens a rich card, so you can see who has it and reserve it in one step.
details: The card shows the item's photo, status, availability, current holder, and due date.
Buttons reserve the item or open its full page.
Numbered battery labels now resolve to the right battery family when scanned or searched.

title: Camera firmware tracking
summary: Camera pages show whether firmware is current, and admins hear about new releases without checking manually.
details: Camera pages show installed and latest firmware with a color badge.
Admins get a notification when a newer firmware version is released for watched gear.

title: iOS Settings hub
summary: The iPhone Profile tab becomes a full Settings hub, bringing notification and account controls to parity with the web.
details: Settings groups account, schedule, notifications, appearance, and tools.
Notifications holds permission recovery, pause, channels, and the same category toggles as the web.
Account & Security lets you change your password and sign out other devices.
Tapping a shift notification opens Schedule to that event.

title: Faster item entry and shorter QR codes
summary: Adding gear takes fewer required fields, and new QR codes are shorter and easier to read on labels.
details: Only asset tag, category, location, and QR code are required; other details can be filled in later.
Add item suggests the next asset tag in a family as you type and can save a photo right after creation.
New QR codes are eight characters long, and existing labels keep working.
The QR dialog downloads a PNG for printing and confirms before replacing a code.
Item detail has grouped sections, an Attachments tab, and Reserve buttons that explain what's blocking them.

title: Refreshed booking creation
summary: Creating a reservation or checkout is calmer and more direct on both web and iPhone, with events filling in the details for you.
details: Creation leads with the event or booking title, with simpler field groups and compact selected-gear chips.
iOS reservations support scan-to-add, battery quantities, and a Confirm step before reserving.
On iPhone, link up to three upcoming events and the title, location, and times fill in automatically.
The requester picker shows photos with you pinned first, and changing the start time keeps the booking length.
iOS booking rows show live pickup and due countdowns plus a kiosk next-step banner.

title: Invitation-only onboarding
summary: New accounts are created by invitation only, so every person sets their own password when they sign up.
details: One Onboard users dialog handles single and bulk invites, flagging duplicates and existing accounts before sending.
An onboarding status page shows pending, stale, and claimed invitations.
Staff can copy a sign-up link for an unclaimed invitation or remove a stale one.

title: Clearer iOS labels and error recovery
summary: The iOS app trades icon-only controls for clear labels and recovers gracefully when something fails or a list is empty.
details: Buttons and tabs use visible labels like Claim shift, Assign person, Create Reservation, and My Gear.
Empty and failed lists offer Clear search, Show all, New Reservation, or Retry.
Failed scans can be retried, and the scanner explains camera access and offers typed entry.
Booking Detail explains when editing is locked, and edits warn if someone else changed the reservation first.
Trade Board, favorite, and mark-as-read failures show clear errors instead of silently reverting.
VoiceOver labels, tap targets, and Dynamic Type support improved across Schedule and Items.

title: Roster onboarding
summary: Staff can invite a whole roster at once and see who has signed up, which makes start-of-semester onboarding much faster.
details: One Onboard users dialog handles single and bulk invites, previewing pasted email and role lists.
The preview flags duplicates, invalid emails, and existing accounts before anything is sent.
An onboarding status page shows pending, stale, and claimed invitations, with who sent and claimed each.
Staff can copy a phone-friendly sign-up link or remove a stale invitation before reissuing it.

title: Semester class conflicts and call times
summary: Availability now follows the academic calendar, and staff can fine-tune call times for a single slot or person.
details: Weekly class blocks take semester start and end dates.
Students can add one-off conflicts like exams, and staff can manage them from profiles.
Staff can set or clear a call time for a slot or one person, and everyone sees the same effective time.
The assignment grid filters to conflicted, open, or clean slots, with conflict notes beside each person.
Event crews show each person's availability conflicts.

title: First-login password on iOS
summary: People given a temporary password or an admin reset can set a new one directly in the iPhone app.
details: Password setup shows a live requirements checklist.
The sign-in screen links invited users to account creation again.

title: Item families in kits
summary: Kits can now include item families, such as batteries, with a quantity instead of only individual items.
details: The kit page searches active item families at the kit's location and skips ones already added.
Each family is added with its own quantity, from 1 to 999.

title: Multi-day events
summary: Manually added events can span several days or run all day, and bookings linked to them cover the whole event.
details: Multi-day all-day events appear on every day they cover.
Linking one to a reservation or checkout sets the booking to cover the full span.

title: Calendar sync status
summary: Staff can see at a glance whether calendar feeds are current, and admins hear about it when syncing keeps failing.
details: Schedule shows whether each calendar feed is fresh, stale, disabled, or failing.
Admins get an alert after repeated daily sync failures, and the issue appears in Fix Today.
Manual syncs in Calendar Sources report the actual events and shifts updated.

title: Conflict and battery stock warnings
summary: Booking warnings stay visible through review, and battery quantities stay accurate while you book.
details: Conflict and turnaround warnings carry through to the review step, and the new booking is highlighted.
iOS booking detail and reservation creation flag gear that conflicts with another booking.
The battery picker shows requested versus available and adjusts if stock drops.
Battery Ops can add units and adjust counts with a required reason.
Two bookings claiming the same gear at once now get a clear conflict message.

title: iOS Schedule availability
summary: Class conflicts, sport filters, and crew coverage come to the iOS Schedule, so staffing works the same on iPhone as on the web.
details: Students can add and delete weekly class conflicts from their profile.
The assign picker shows who has a class conflict, while still allowing staff to assign them.
Filter the Schedule by sport in both list and calendar views.
Staff see a filled-versus-needed crew chip on each event.

title: Admin policies, audit log, and exports
summary: Admins can set checkout and reservation rules, review system activity, and pull data exports from Settings.
details: Checkout Policies set default loan length and overdue grace.
Reservation Rules set how far ahead people can book, no-show expiry, and a per-person reservation limit.
An Audit Log page shows a live, filterable feed of system actions.
Data Export downloads Items, Users, Licenses, Bookings, and Audit Log CSVs from one place.

title: Self-service settings
summary: Everyone can manage their own profile, password, sessions, and notifications without asking an admin.
details: Edit your name, phone, primary area, title, Athletics email, Slack handle, and photo.
Change your password and sign out other devices individually or all at once.
Toggle due reminders, overdue alerts, reservation updates, and license expiry reminders.
You're notified when assigned a shift, a request is approved, you're removed, or your call time changes.

title: Staff and Student slots
summary: Crews now track Staff and Student slots separately, so events are staffed with the right mix and call times.
details: Crew defaults and events track Staff and Student slots, with shift-level and per-person call times.
Sports settings set Staff and Student minimum crew per area and for home or away games.
Expanded Schedule rows add Staff or Student slots and remove assignments inline.
Staff can edit an event's title, home or away, and location, and edits survive calendar sync.
Confirmations for shift actions say exactly what happens, such as a slot reopening.

title: Quick search for pages and settings
summary: Quick search now finds pages, settings, and reports you can open, not just records.
details: Results include the pages, settings, and reports your role can access.
Example searches appear when nothing matches, and search keeps working if one source fails.

title: Product photo search
summary: Staff can find a product photo by name and attach it to an item without leaving the app.
details: Search for a product photo and save the one you pick as the item image.
Item families use the same image search.
Photos from imported items are copied into the app's own storage so they keep displaying.
Attachment dialogs are searchable, explain what can be attached, and warn about busy items.

title: Guides become Resources
summary: Guides moved to a new Resources page with a directory-style layout, and old links redirect automatically.
details: A filter rail, search and sort toolbar, and removable filter chips make resources easier to find.
Saving, editing, and uploading images in guides shows clearer errors.

title: Trade Board and grid redesign
summary: The Trade Board and assignment grid focus on what's actionable, and event colors and titles are consistent everywhere.
details: Trades show as compact cards with event, shift time, area, people, and notes.
Trades for shifts that have already started can no longer be posted, claimed, or approved.
The assignment grid shows upcoming events only, groups slots by area, and adds or removes slots in place.
Home is green, away orange, and neutral gray in every view, with one shared title format.
Hiding an event from the Schedule offers Undo.

title: Fix Today list and kiosk status
summary: Admins get one daily list of what needs attention, and stale pickups clean themselves up.
details: Fix Today lists overdue checkouts, pending pickups, offline kiosks, flagged items, low batteries, and expiring licenses.
Kiosk Devices in Settings shows each kiosk's online status and open pickups, and clears stuck pickups.
Pickups left unclaimed two days after their start are canceled and the gear is released.
The kiosk home still loads if one section fails.

title: Item families
summary: Similar items now group into families, so batteries and other counted gear can be browsed, reserved, and audited by model.
details: Batteries and other unit- or quantity-tracked gear appear as single rows in Items with their own pages.
New items offer Standard, Units, or Quantity tracking.
Selecting a camera recommends compatible batteries, with exact units scanned at kiosk pickup.
Kiosk pickup and return show how many battery units are needed and scanned.
Missing Units adds a battery audit by unit number and family, with recent checkout history.

title: Badge gallery and custom badges
summary: Profiles on web and iPhone get a full badge gallery, and admins can create custom badges for staff recognition.
details: The profile Badges tab has collection shelves and filters for earned, locked, manual, and rare badges.
iPhone profiles show the gallery with detail sheets, and badge notifications open the right profile.
Admins can create a custom badge while awarding it, with a live preview, and reuse it later.
Staff can revoke an award, and badge details use a trophy-case layout.

title: iPhone Home Next Up queue
summary: iPhone Home is rebuilt around a Next Up list of your own work, so the most urgent task is always first.
details: A compact triage strip sits above Next Up: overdue gear, items due today, pickups, reservations, and shifts.
Each event you're working shows as one row with gear pickup and call times, or a prompt to reserve gear.
Re-tapping the Home tab resets the view.

title: Awaiting Pickup status
summary: Reserved gear that's ready to collect now has its own Awaiting Pickup status, so pending pickups never look like active checkouts.
details: Items, checkouts, and the Checkouts tab show Awaiting Pickup with matching colors and actions.
Web and iPhone Home list reservations waiting for pickup, turning amber once the pickup time passes.
Future reservations no longer appear as active.
Overdue and late-pickup times on iPhone Home update every minute.

title: Guides knowledge base
summary: Guides become a searchable Creative knowledge base for how-tos, contacts, and reference info.
details: Guides use Markdown, search inside the body, and offer starter templates for contacts, SOPs, and troubleshooting.
A live Contacts view lists current team members with photo, role, phone, and area.
Admins can feature guides and target them to roles or areas, and editors can mark guides verified.
Headings have shareable links, code blocks and tables have copy buttons, and articles have a sticky table of contents.

title: Badges for gear and shifts
summary: Everyone now earns badges for gear and shift activity, and admins can recognize great work with manual awards.
details: Badges are earned automatically for checkouts, on-time returns, kiosk scans, and shift trades.
Badges show rarity, some stay hidden until earned, and goals show real progress.
New awards arrive as notifications that link to your badges.
A Badges report shows award totals, recent awards, a leaderboard, and distribution, with CSV export.

title: Kiosk scanning and feedback
summary: Kiosk checkout, pickup, and return give clearer feedback and make mistakes easy to undo.
details: Scan results appear over the camera view, scroll to the latest item, and are announced to VoiceOver.
Each scanned item has a remove button, checkout adds undo, and a Done screen returns home immediately.
Pickup can't be confirmed until every serialized item is scanned, by asset tag, QR code, or serial number.
When completion fails, the kiosk shows the actual problem instead of a false success.
The idle screen, roster, and student hub show photos, item summaries, and when data last updated.
Activation accepts a pasted code, and deactivating a kiosk asks for confirmation.

title: iPhone directory, bookings, and scanning
summary: The iOS app adds a Users directory and overdue report, plus faster scanning and richer item and booking screens.
details: A Users tab lets you search people with role and inactive filters and open their profiles.
Staff get an overdue report with a per-person list sorted by overdue time.
Bookings add a Mine filter, a live due-back countdown, and +1 day, +3 days, and +1 week extend shortcuts.
Item Detail shows availability at a glance, the QR code, accessories, and a Reserve Equipment button.
The Scan tab adds a flashlight, a Type code option, and fast repeat scanning.
Profile holds notification preferences and a light or dark theme choice, and VoiceOver reads rows clearly.

title: Smarter booking creation
summary: Creating a booking flags turnaround risks and low batteries up front, and finished bookings stay out of daily work.
details: The equipment step brings back scan-to-add and flags gear that's no longer available.
Bookings show a Back before time and warn about short turnarounds, location moves, or recent damage.
Selecting a camera warns when compatible batteries are running low.
The Bookings page has Active and Past views, and tabs are saved in the link.
Damage and loss reports can include a photo.

title: License history and bulk renewal
summary: Software license management takes fewer steps for admins and is more transparent for everyone.
details: Open a history of when you claimed and returned licenses, without showing old codes.
Admins can renew expiring codes in one step and see a pool summary of active codes and upcoming expirations.

title: Inventory cleanup tools
summary: Staff get tools to find and fix gaps in the catalog, plus a cleaner Settings home and reorganized item pages.
details: A hygiene checklist flags missing categories, images, or scan codes, with links straight to each fix.
Item pages have Schedule, Insights, History, and Attachments tabs, and camera pages list SD cards by slot.
Right-click an item row to open it, copy its tag, favorite it, or print a label.
Staff and admins can add, rename, and deactivate departments in Settings.
Settings opens on a role-aware overview with a Resume button for your last page.

title: Numbered batteries and Battery Ops
summary: Each numbered battery now has its own QR label, so the kiosk knows exactly which units go out and come back.
details: Kiosk pickup and return accept each battery's label, and pickup waits until all planned batteries are scanned.
The kiosk explains when a battery is the wrong type, checked out elsewhere, already scanned, or retired.
Battery Ops shows available, checked-out, and missing units per family, with low-stock warnings by camera.
Canceled checkouts return bulk quantities to stock, and quantity-only items show accurate availability.

title: Schedule readiness and trade emails
summary: Staff can see at a glance which events need crew and fill them inline, and trade participants get email updates.
details: The Schedule shows open slots, fully staffed events, your shifts, open trades, and the next call time.
Expanded events show every area and slot so staff can fill open spots inline.
A Needs staff filter and open-slot counts highlight under-covered events.
Dashboard upcoming events show crew coverage, call times, and open-slot warnings.
You get an email when your trade is claimed, approved, declined, or completed.

title: iOS Liquid Glass and scanning
summary: The iOS app adopts the Liquid Glass look, and scanning gets a proper results sheet.
details: Buttons, search, and the tab bar adopt the Liquid Glass style.
Scan results open in a sheet with haptics, a camera permission prompt, and manual code entry for VoiceOver users.

title: Accessibility improvements
summary: Keyboard access, screen reader labels, field error announcements, and contrast improved across the web app, and motion respects your device setting.
details: Animations tone down when your device is set to reduce motion.
People without a profile photo get a consistent colored initials avatar.

title: Team profiles and org chart
summary: Profiles hold the details staff need about each team member, with an org chart and an easier-to-filter roster.
details: Profiles add title, Athletics email, start date, manager, graduation year, and apparel sizes.
Student year is worked out automatically, and an org chart view shows reporting lines.
Filter people by year, sport, and area, and export the list to CSV.
Activity entries describe what changed in plain language and link to the record.

title: Items list upgrades
summary: The Items list shows due dates, works as its own filter, and makes bulk actions safer.
details: Checked-out items show when they're due or how overdue they are.
Status counts above the list act as filters, and a Compact or Comfortable density choice is remembered.
Select every matching item across pages, and undo a bulk retire for a few seconds.
The iOS Items list filters by several statuses at once.

title: Notes on bookings
summary: Checkouts and bookings can carry notes, shown at review, and multi-event bookings list each event's date and home or away.
details: Notes are optional and are saved with booking drafts.
Multi-event bookings tag the earliest event as Primary.
Title, requester, location, and dates are clearly marked as required.

title: Shift calendar subscriptions
summary: Students and staff can subscribe to their shifts in Apple, Google, or Outlook calendar with a personal link.
details: The feed stays in sync with schedule changes, so you never need to subscribe again.
On iPhone, a button on the Schedule tab opens the calendar subscribe sheet.
You can generate a new link from your profile, replacing the old one.

title: Weekly class conflicts
summary: Students can share the weekly times they can't work, so staff see a warning before assigning them.
details: Students add recurring weekly class times from their profile.
Staff see a conflict warning when assigning someone during a class.

title: Monthly assignment grid
summary: Staff can fill a whole month of shifts from one grid instead of opening events one at a time.
details: The grid shows events by area, with sport and area filters.
Crew can be assigned and changed inline from an event's crew table.
Students post shifts for trade from the Schedule, and a My Trades filter shows their own.

title: iPhone shift editing and dashboard
summary: Staff can manage shifts from the iPhone, and the iOS dashboard becomes interactive.
details: Approve requests, change call times, and duplicate, replace, or delete shifts.
Tap, long-press, and act on dashboard rows, with staff-only sections.
Home events in the next few days show a weather forecast.
Scan legacy sticker codes and link them to items.

title: Renamed to Wisconsin Creative
summary: The app now goes by Wisconsin Creative on the web and iPhone.
details: The new name appears in the sidebar, sign-in pages, page titles, and email footers.
The iPhone sign-in screen was redesigned with a card layout and a show password option.

title: Personal settings and notification controls
summary: Settings opens to everyone, so each person can choose how the app looks and how they hear about gear and shifts.
details: Appearance offers light, dark, or system theme and four text sizes.
A Notifications page lets you pause alerts for an hour, a day, or a week.
Turn email or push notifications on or off individually.

title: Schedule and crew on iPhone
summary: The iPhone app gains the Schedule and Trade Board, and staff can manage crew for an event without opening the web app.
details: See events and shifts in a list or calendar, with a Today button and month swiping.
Post, claim, and cancel shift trades, with confirmations before posting or cancelling.
Staff can add shifts, assign students from the sport roster, and remove assignments.
Students can request open shift slots from an event.

title: Admin settings overhaul
summary: Settings is reorganized for admins, with a new Locations page, feed testing for calendars, and faster tools for managing who can sign up.
details: Settings tabs are grouped, role-aware, searchable with Command-K, and remember where you left off.
Locations lets admins add, rename, mark home venues, and deactivate locations without breaking existing records.
Calendar Sources can test a feed and preview its events before saving.
Allowed Emails accepts a pasted list and shows counts for all, pending, and claimed invites.
Locations and Allowed Emails rows show who last edited them and when.
Kiosk iPads can be re-paired from Settings and show Offline when they stop checking in.

title: Native iPad kiosk
summary: The kiosk moves from the web to a native iPad app, giving the gear room a faster, more dependable self-service station.
details: Handles checkout, pickup, and return with the iPad camera as the scanner.
Scans are kept if the screen times out mid-checkout.
Returns now require a kiosk scan too, with a staff override on the web.

title: Native iPhone app
summary: Wisconsin Creative arrives on iPhone as a native app for bookings, items, scanning, and search, with push alerts as gear comes due.
details: Push notifications arrive as gear comes due and becomes overdue, and tapping one opens the booking.
Items, bookings, and schedule show saved data instantly and refresh in the background.
Reserve from an item with that item and its location already filled in.
Star favorite items and filter the list to just your favorites.
Login adds Forgot password, iCloud Keychain autofill, and ignores stray spaces in your email.
Push permission is explained before the system prompt, and expired sessions return to Login.

title: Bookings across multiple events
summary: One reservation or checkout can now cover several events, such as a weekend series, so crews stop creating a booking per game.
details: The booking window spans from the first linked event to the last automatically.
Each event page lists every booking tied to it, even when another event is the main one.
Reservations send notifications when booked, ready for pickup, or cancelled.

title: Shared software license pool
summary: Staff and students can sign out a Photo Mechanic license code from a shared pool instead of tracking codes by hand.
details: Claim a code, copy it, and release it when you are done.
Each code supports two holders and shows its expiry date.
Reminders go out before a code lapses, and staff can export the pool to a spreadsheet.

title: Smarter crew scheduling
summary: Scheduling now accounts for when students can work and who travels, and can fill shifts automatically from rosters.
details: Auto-assign fills shifts from sport and area rosters, with conflict checks.
Students can block out times they're unavailable, such as classes.
Away travel rosters let staff choose who travels, with default travelers.
Post-event attendance records who worked, and past events archive automatically.
Staff can add events that aren't on a synced calendar.
Trade Board notifies the right people, flags class conflicts, and expires old trades.

title: Team how-to guides
summary: A home for the team's how-tos. Staff write and publish guides for gear and workflows, and everyone can read them from the sidebar.
details: Write guides in a rich editor with images that upload directly.
Longer guides get a table of contents sidebar.
Wider editor and reader layouts make screenshots easier to follow.

title: Self-service gear kiosk
summary: The iPad kiosk becomes a full self-service station: people tap their photo, check out gear, and return it by scanning.
details: Sessions time out automatically so the next person starts fresh.
Reservations show when gear is ready for pickup, and pickup scanning happens at the kiosk.

title: Step-by-step booking wizard
summary: Creating a checkout or reservation is now a guided three-step page that ends by taking you straight to scanning the gear.
details: A rebuilt equipment picker, quick-add events, pickup location, and a clear summary before you confirm.
New checkouts go directly to scanning.
Booking details add an Equipment tab for editing gear and scanning returns.
Extend a booking with quick presets or a custom date and time.
Bookings add an All tab and a switch between cards and a table.

title: Refreshed design and missing-details tool
summary: A bolder Wisconsin Athletics look across the app, plus a guided tool for cleaning up incomplete item records.
details: Dashboard, schedule, items, users, and sidebar get refreshed styling and better text contrast.
User photos appear consistently across the app.
Item pages lead with a bolder asset tag and name, with key properties grouped beneath.
A fill-in tool walks through items missing a category or department and suggests values.

title: Neutral-site games
summary: Games at neutral venues are detected and labeled across the schedule and bookings, so they no longer read as home or away.
details: Neutral-site events get their own color in Calendar view.
A game listed as vs at a venue that isn't a home venue is marked Neutral.
Schedule filters add a Neutral option alongside Home and Away.

title: Kiosk mode on iPad
summary: A first kiosk mode lets students check gear out and back in themselves at a shared iPad station.
details: Admins add, edit, and remove kiosk iPads from Settings.
Idle screens show who currently has gear out.

title: Bulk battery tracking
summary: Batteries and other bulk stock are easier to track and harder to lose.
details: Bulk items can be part of kits.
A loss-by-user report shows where bulk gear goes missing.
Bookings enforce battery requirements for gear that needs them.

title: Invite-only sign-up
summary: Only invited email addresses can create an account, and each person's role is set when the invite is sent.
details: Admins manage the Allowed Emails list from Settings.
Staff can invite students, while admins can invite any role.
Invitations that have already been used stay on the list.

title: Schedule week view and hours
summary: The Schedule adds a seven-day view and shows students how much they've worked.
details: Week view shows events by time with coverage dots, an all-day row, and week-to-week navigation.
See your hours and shifts worked this week and this month.
Filter by home or away, and staff can hide events that don't need crew.

title: Scan feedback and checklist
summary: Scanning gives clearer confirmation, so you know a scan worked without looking at the screen.
details: Distinct sounds and vibrations for success, error, and completion.
A compact camera and an image checklist show what's been scanned.
Scan lookup opens a panel with the item's photo, status, and quick actions.

title: Condition photos and scan-only returns
summary: Checkouts and check-ins now record what the gear looked like, and returns are done by scanning.
details: Completing a checkout or check-in asks for camera photos of the gear's condition.
Flag an item as damaged or lost while checking it in.

title: Book from anywhere
summary: Booking buttons on the dashboard, events, and items open booking creation in place with details already filled in.
details: Reserve or check out straight from an item's page.
Dashboard and event buttons prefill the event.

title: Beta release
summary: The first official Beta of Wisconsin Creative, ready for daily use by the creative team. It brings reservations, checkouts, scheduling, kits, reports, and search together in one app.
details: Reservations and checkouts require QR scans, support partial check-in and drafts, and flag missing pieces like batteries.
Calendars sync daily, shifts are generated from sport settings, and the Trade Board handles swaps.
Students see their own gear while staff see daily operations, with sport and location filters.
Due-date reminders arrive in the app and by email, escalating to staff when gear stays overdue.
Reports cover checkouts, overdue gear, utilization, scans, and history, with charts and drill-downs.
Dark mode, loading placeholders, and phone-sized tap targets throughout.

title: Home and away venues
summary: Events now know where they are. Calendar venue names map to app locations, and home venues label each event home or away.
details: Admins map calendar venue names to locations so events land at the right place.
Venues can be marked as home.

title: Search and report charts
summary: Search becomes faster and broader, and reports gain charts.
details: Search runs as you type, includes people, and remembers recent searches.
Command-K answers who has my gear.
Reports gain charts for utilization, checkout trends, overdue gear, and scans.

title: Item favorites and export
summary: The Items list gets faster to work with.
details: Star items and filter to just your favorites.
Staff can download the filtered Items view as a spreadsheet.
An inventory summary sits above the list, and hidden columns stay hidden.

title: Wisconsin branding
summary: The app adopts Wisconsin typography and the Motion W logo, with cleaner, quieter dashboard cards.
details: Durations read in full, and upcoming events use full sport names.
Headings use Gotham, and the Motion W replaces the old mark in the sidebar, sign-in page, and browser icon.
Wisconsin red is saved for brand moments like the active sidebar item, overdue banner, and notification badges.

title: Gear kits
summary: Kits group gear that goes out together, so a standard camera package can be booked in one step.
details: Create named kits per location and add or remove members.
See each kit's availability and archive kits you no longer use.
Choose a kit when creating a booking and see it labeled on the booking.

title: Bookings page and sidebar
summary: Checkouts and reservations now share one Bookings page, and the sidebar surfaces what needs attention.
details: Bookings lists both types with a card view, overdue bookings first.
New bookings open in a side panel without leaving the page.
The equipment picker searches across all sections with keyboard navigation and photo thumbnails.
The sidebar collapses and shows counts for overdue gear and unread notifications.
The dashboard shows recent activity as a chart and remembers saved filter views.

title: One Schedule page
summary: Events and shifts now live together on a single Schedule page, so crew coverage is visible right next to each event.
details: List and calendar views with coverage badges and full sport names.
A My Shifts filter, and events expand to show who is working each area.
Staff can add or remove shifts per event and assign anyone from an avatar picker.
Manual shift edits are kept when the calendar syncs.

title: Unified booking detail page
summary: Checkouts and reservations share one detail page with clearer status, actions, and progress.
details: Activity history reads in plain language.
Edit a booking's title inline.

title: Rebuilt Items list
summary: The Items list is rebuilt for speed, with broader search and better tools for working with many items.
details: Search covers tags, brand, model, serial, notes, category, location, and department.
Sort, filter by department, choose columns, and act on rows from a menu.
Create items in a side panel with QR codes you can generate or scan.
Select several items for bulk actions, and use a card view on phones.

title: Item and profile photos
summary: Items and people can now have photos, which makes the right gear and the right person easier to spot.
details: Add an item photo by uploading a file or pasting a link.
Profile photos appear on the dashboard and sidebar.

title: Event command center
summary: Each event gets one page showing its crew, who has gear, and who is still missing gear.
details: Staff can nudge crew members who haven't picked up gear.
Gear booked for an event links to the person's shift, so the page shows each crew member's gear status.
Creating a checkout for an event shows your shift area and time for that event.

title: Users directory redesign
summary: The Users directory gets real search and filters, and each person gets a profile page.
details: Profile pages have Info and Activity tabs with phone, primary area, and sport rosters.
Mobile-friendly cards replace the table on phones.

title: Due-date reminders
summary: Checkouts now send in-app and email reminders before gear is due, when it is due, and when it is overdue.
details: Overdue reminders also go out by email.
A reports hub shows who tends to return gear late.

title: Shift scheduling and Trade Board
summary: Every synced event now gets shifts. Staff assign crew by area, students pick up open slots, and the Trade Board handles swaps.
details: Admins set how many people each area needs for home and away games per sport.
Post a shift you can't work, and a teammate can claim it with staff approval.
Getting a shift sends a gear-up reminder, and My Shifts on the dashboard shows gear status.
Email notifications when you're assigned to or removed from a shift.
Scheduling guards against overlapping assignments.

title: Reference numbers, drafts, and accessories
summary: Bookings get short reference numbers and saved drafts, and accessories can travel with their main item.
details: Every booking gets a short, searchable reference number shown in lists and details.
Unfinished bookings are saved as drafts you can resume or discard from the dashboard.
Accessories link to a parent item and are grouped under it in the Items list.

title: Bulk inventory
summary: Pooled gear like batteries and cables can be tracked by quantity, or by numbered unit so missing pieces can be traced.
details: Create items as individually tracked gear or as bulk stock.
Give each bulk unit its own number, like battery #7, to spot losses.

title: Usage reports
summary: Report pages show how gear is used and where it goes, with charts, filters, and date ranges.
details: Covers utilization, checkout activity, overdue gear, missing units, scans, and audit history.
Reports are organized into tabs, with metric cards above the charts.
Each report shows a clear empty state or error when there's nothing to load.

title: Spreadsheet import with column mapping
summary: Importing gear from a CSV is more reliable for large files and shows exactly what will happen first.
details: Match spreadsheet columns to item fields.
Preview which rows will be created, updated, or skipped before importing.

title: Scan modes
summary: The scan page can look up an item, add gear to a checkout, or check gear back in.
details: Lookup mode shows an item's status, holder, and location in a sheet without leaving the scan page.
Checkout and check-in scans track progress item by item and celebrate when everything is scanned.
Students can scan their own gear out and back in without staff help.

title: iPhone-friendly web app
summary: Pages are reworked for phone screens, and the web app can be installed on your home screen.
details: Larger tap targets across the app.
Students get a simpler sidebar, can scan their own gear, and see it highlighted in My Gear.
Dark mode follows your device setting or can be set by hand.
Search across the app from anywhere with a keyboard shortcut.

title: Operations dashboard
summary: The dashboard shows what is out and what is due, split into your gear and team activity.
details: Countdowns change color as due times approach.
Overdue items are called out in a banner at the top.
A stat strip and upcoming events round out the view.

title: Reservations and pickup
summary: Gear can be reserved ahead of time and turned into a checkout at pickup.
details: Duplicate an existing reservation to start a new one with the same gear.
Search, filter, and sort checkouts and reservations.

title: Items list and detail pages
summary: Browse all gear with filters, then open any item to see its bookings, info, and full history.
details: Staff can edit item details inline.
Organize gear into categories.
The History tab shows everything that has happened to an item.

title: Checkout workflow
summary: Checkouts get a real workflow: pick gear by section, return it in parts, and see conflicts before they happen.
details: An equipment picker groups gear by section, with kits shown first.
Return some items now and the rest later.
Warnings show when an item is already booked or a piece like a battery is missing.
Open any booking to change its gear, extend it, or cancel it.
Checkouts link to events and can be filtered by sport.

title: Wisconsin Creative, first build
summary: The first working build lays the foundation: an equipment inventory, synced athletics calendars, QR labels, and accounts. It is early groundwork, not yet in daily use.
details: Track each item's location, status, and who has it.
Game and event calendars sync into the app.
Scan gear with a phone camera and print QR labels.
Import existing gear from a spreadsheet with a preview first.
Account registration, profiles, and a notification center.
